grammar_points.name: 〜のでしょう (no deshou: I suppose; probably)

explanation.en:
How it works: のでしょう (no deshou) combines the explanatory の (no) with でしょう (deshou, 'probably/I suppose'). It expresses a polite guess or supposition with an explanatory tone.

Example from this song: 解いたのでしょう (toita no deshou) = 'I suppose (you) solved it' — from 解く (toku, 'to solve') → 解いた (toita, past) + のでしょう (no deshou)

More examples:
• 疲れたのでしょう (tsukareta no deshou, 'I suppose you're tired') — from 疲れる (tsukareru, 'to get tired')
• 知らなかったのでしょう (shiranakatta no deshou, 'I suppose they didn't know')
• 難しいのでしょう (muzukashii no deshou, 'it's probably difficult')

Note: でしょう alone = 'probably.' のでしょう = 'probably (and here's why I think so).' The の adds explanatory nuance. Casual form: のだろう (no darou) / んだろう (n darou).

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 解く (toku, 'to solve') → 解いた (toita, 'solved') + のでしょう (no deshou, 'I suppose') → 解いたのでしょう (toita no deshou, 'I suppose you solved it')

grammar_points.name: 〜なんかじゃない (nanka janai: it's not something like)

explanation.en:
How it works: なんか (nanka) means 'something like' (dismissive), and じゃない (ja nai) means 'is not.' Together, なんかじゃない denies that something is trivial or dismissible.

Example from this song: 勇気なんかじゃない (yuuki nanka ja nai) = 'it's not something trivial like courage' — from 勇気 (yuuki, 'courage'). The speaker insists it's something deeper than mere courage.

More examples:
• 嘘なんかじゃない (uso nanka ja nai, 'it's not a lie or anything') — defending the truth
• 遊びなんかじゃない (asobi nanka ja nai, 'it's not just playing around') — insisting it's serious
• 弱さなんかじゃない (yowasa nanka ja nai, 'it's not weakness') — rejecting a label

Note: なんか is casual and slightly dismissive. Using なんかじゃない is emphatic denial — 'it's NOT just some...' It shows emotional investment in correcting a misunderstanding.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 勇気 (yuuki, 'courage') + なんか (nanka, 'something like') + じゃない (ja nai, 'is not') → 勇気なんかじゃない (yuuki nanka ja nai, 'it's not something trivial like courage')

grammar_points.name: 〜じゃなくたって (janakutatte: even if it's not)

explanation.en:
How it works: じゃなくたって (ja nakutatte) is the casual concessive form of ではなくても (de wa nakutemo), meaning 'even if it's not.' たって is a casual version of ても.

Example from this song: 虹の彼方じゃなくたって (niji no kanata ja nakutatte) = 'even if it's not beyond the rainbow' — the speaker says the destination doesn't have to be somewhere magical

More examples:
• 完璧じゃなくたっていい (kanpeki ja nakutatte ii, 'it doesn't have to be perfect')
• 一番じゃなくたって (ichiban ja nakutatte, 'even if you're not number one')
• 大人じゃなくたってわかる (otona ja nakutatte wakaru, 'even kids can understand / even if you're not an adult')

Note: The casual chain: ではなくても → じゃなくても → じゃなくたって. たって is very casual/spoken. This pattern is encouraging — 'even if things aren't ideal, it's still OK.'

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 虹の彼方 (niji no kanata, 'beyond the rainbow') + じゃなくたって (ja nakutatte, 'even if it's not') → 虹の彼方じゃなくたって (niji no kanata ja nakutatte, 'even if it's not beyond the rainbow')

grammar_points.name: 〜だけだ (dake da: it's just that; only)

explanation.en:
How it works: だけだ (dake da) limits the extent of something — 'it was only...' or 'nothing more than...' It downplays or simplifies what happened.

Example from this song: 強がっていただけだ (tsuyogatte ita dake da) = 'I was only putting on a brave face' — from 強がる (tsuyogaru, 'to act tough') → 強がっていた (tsuyogatte ita, 'was acting tough') + だけだ (dake da)

More examples:
• 聞いただけだ (kiita dake da, 'I only asked') — from 聞く (kiku, 'to ask')
• ちょっと疲れただけだ (chotto tsukareta dake da, 'I'm just a little tired')
• 知りたかっただけだ (shiritakatta dake da, 'I just wanted to know')

Note: だけ = 'only/just.' だけだ at the end of a sentence is explanatory — it's saying 'it was nothing more than X.' Very useful for downplaying or explaining away something.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 強がる (tsuyogaru, 'to bluff') → 強がっていた (tsuyogatte ita, 'was bluffing') + だけだ (dake da, 'it's just') → 強がっていただけだ (tsuyogatte ita dake da, 'was only bluffing')

grammar_points.name: 〜てくれる (te kureru: to do for me)

explanation.en:
How it works: Attach くれる (kureru) to a verb's te-form to express that someone does something beneficial for the speaker. It carries a sense of gratitude.

Example from this song: あなたがくれた (anata ga kureta) = 'what you gave me' — from くれる (kureru, 'to give to me') → くれた (kureta, past). Here it stands alone rather than as a compound verb.

More examples:
• 教えてくれた (oshiete kureta, 'taught me') — from 教える (oshieru, 'to teach')
• 助けてくれてありがとう (tasukete kurete arigatou, 'thank you for helping me')
• 信じてくれた (shinjite kureta, 'believed in me') — from 信じる (shinjiru, 'to believe')

Note: くれる means someone gives/does something beneficial TO the speaker. あげる means the speaker gives/does for someone else. This distinction is uniquely Japanese and reflects awareness of social relationships.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: あなた (anata, 'you') + が (ga) + くれた (kureta, 'gave to me') → あなたがくれた (anata ga kureta, 'what you gave me')

explanation.en: Group-1 verbs swap final -u for -ou: 進む → 進もう ('let's advance'), 急ぐ → 急ごう, 乗る → 乗ろう. Group-2 verbs use 〜よう: 見る → 見よう. Used to propose actions to oneself or a group.
explanation.es: Verbos del Grupo 1 cambian -u final por -ou: 進む → 進もう ('avancemos'), 急ぐ → 急ごう, 乗る → 乗ろう. Grupo 2 usa 〜よう: 見る → 見よう. Para proponer acciones.
explanation.pt-BR: Verbos do Grupo 1 trocam -u final por -ou: 進む → 進もう ('vamos avançar'), 急ぐ → 急ごう, 乗る → 乗ろう. Grupo 2 usa 〜よう: 見る → 見よう. Para propor ações.

explanation.en: Past form + ら expresses 'when X happens / once X is done / if X'. 上げたら 'once we lift', 来たら 'when X comes', 重ねたら 'if we stack'. The most flexible Japanese conditional — works for both factual and hypothetical contexts.
explanation.es: Forma pasada + ら expresa 'cuando X / en cuanto X / si X'. 上げたら 'en cuanto levantemos', 来たら 'cuando venga', 重ねたら 'si apilamos'. La condicional más flexible.
explanation.pt-BR: Forma passada + ら expressa 'quando X / assim que X / se X'. 上げたら 'assim que levantarmos', 来たら 'quando vier', 重ねたら 'se empilharmos'. A condicional mais flexível.

explanation.en: Verb -e-stem + ば creates a hypothetical 'if X'. 集まれば 'if (they) gather'. Tends to express natural/general consequences rather than one-off events. Common in proverbs and song lyrics.
explanation.es: Raíz -e del verbo + ば forma hipótesis 'si X'. 集まれば 'si se reúnen'. Expresa consecuencias naturales o generales. Común en proverbios y letras.
explanation.pt-BR: Radical -e do verbo + ば forma hipótese 'se X'. 集まれば 'se (eles) se reunirem'. Expressa consequências naturais ou gerais. Comum em provérbios e letras.

explanation.en: Noun + だらけ means 'covered in / full of (something undesirable)'. 傷だらけの航海 'a battered voyage'; 泥だらけ 'covered in mud'. Carries a negative connotation.
explanation.es: Sustantivo + だらけ significa 'lleno de / cubierto de (algo no deseado)'. 傷だらけの航海 'travesía llena de cicatrices'. Connotación negativa.
explanation.pt-BR: Substantivo + だらけ significa 'cheio de / coberto de (algo indesejável)'. 傷だらけの航海 'viagem cheia de cicatrizes'. Conotação negativa.

explanation.en: 〜ちゃう = 〜てしまう ('do completely / end up doing'). The volitional 〜ちゃおう = 〜てしまおう ('let's just go ahead and do it'). 味方にしちゃおう = 'let's just make it our ally'. Adds energy/finality.
explanation.es: 〜ちゃう = 〜てしまう ('hacer del todo'). Volitivo 〜ちゃおう = 'hagámoslo de una vez'. 味方にしちゃおう 'convirtámoslo en aliado de una'. Añade energía/finalidad.
explanation.pt-BR: 〜ちゃう = 〜てしまう ('fazer por completo'). Volitivo 〜ちゃおう = 'vamos logo fazer'. 味方にしちゃおう 'vamos transformar em aliado de uma vez'. Soma energia/finalidade.

explanation.en: だって is the casual equivalent of でも ('even / too'). 気まぐれな空だって 'even the fickle sky'; いつだって 'anytime / even at any time'. Slangier and more emphatic than でも.
explanation.es: だって es equivalente casual de でも ('incluso / hasta'). 気まぐれな空だって 'hasta el cielo voluble'; いつだって 'en cualquier momento'. Más coloquial que でも.
explanation.pt-BR: だって é equivalente casual de でも ('até / mesmo'). 気まぐれな空だって 'até o céu volúvel'; いつだって 'a qualquer hora / sempre'. Mais coloquial que でも.

explanation.en: Group-1 verbs swap the final -u for -ou: なる → なろう ('let's become'), 行く → 行こう. Group-2 verbs use 〜よう: 食べる → 食べよう. Used for proposals to oneself or a group: 'let's do X'.
explanation.es: Verbos del Grupo 1 cambian el -u final por -ou: なる → なろう ('volvámonos'), 行く → 行こう. Grupo 2 usa 〜よう: 食べる → 食べよう. Para propuestas: 'hagamos X'.
explanation.pt-BR: Verbos do Grupo 1 trocam o -u final por -ou: なる → なろう ('vamos ser'), 行く → 行こう. Grupo 2 usa 〜よう: 食べる → 食べよう. Para propostas: 'vamos fazer X'.

explanation.en: The plain imperative is a blunt command. Group-1: change -u to -e (遊ぶ → 遊べ 'play!'). Group-2: add -ろ (食べる → 食べろ 'eat!'). Used in shouted/sung speech, fight scenes, and song lyrics for force; rude in normal conversation.
explanation.es: Imperativo plano = orden directa. Grupo 1: cambia -u por -e (遊ぶ → 遊べ '¡juega!'). Grupo 2: añade -ろ (食べる → 食べろ '¡come!'). Usado en escenas de lucha, gritos, letras; grosero en conversación normal.
explanation.pt-BR: Imperativo simples = ordem direta. Grupo 1: troca -u por -e (遊ぶ → 遊べ 'brinque!'). Grupo 2: adiciona -ろ (食べる → 食べろ 'coma!'). Usado em cena de luta, gritos, letras; grosseiro no dia a dia.

explanation.en: Group-1: -u → -aseru (笑う → 笑わせる 'make laugh'). Group-2: -る → -saseru (咲く is Group-1: 咲かせる 'make bloom'). The causative + imperative (笑わせろ, さかせろ, させろ) is a forceful 'make it happen!' command.
explanation.es: Grupo 1: -u → -aseru (笑う → 笑わせる 'hacer reír'). Grupo 2: -る → -saseru. Causativo + imperativo (笑わせろ, させろ) es una orden enérgica '¡hazlo pasar!'.
explanation.pt-BR: Grupo 1: -u → -aseru (笑う → 笑わせる 'fazer rir'). Grupo 2: -る → -saseru. Causativo + imperativo (笑わせろ, させろ) é um comando forte 'faça acontecer!'.

explanation.en: 〜ちゃう = 〜てしまう ('end up doing / do completely'). The imperative 〜ちゃえ is a punchy 'just do it already!' 笑わせちゃえ = 'just go ahead and make them laugh!'. Often pairs with causative for energetic shounen-style commands.
explanation.es: 〜ちゃう = 〜てしまう ('terminar haciendo / hacer del todo'). El imperativo 〜ちゃえ es un '¡hazlo de una!'. 笑わせちゃえ = '¡venga, hazlos reír!'. Suele combinarse con causativo en comandos shounen.
explanation.pt-BR: 〜ちゃう = 〜てしまう ('acabar fazendo / fazer por completo'). O imperativo 〜ちゃえ é um 'vai logo, faz!'. 笑わせちゃえ = 'vai, faça eles rirem!'. Costuma pareiar com causativo para comandos shounen.

grammar_points.name: 〜場合じゃない (this is no time for X)

explanation.en: Plain form + 場合じゃない literally 'is not the case for X' = 'this is no time to X'. 泣いてる場合じゃない = 'no time to be crying'. Often used to push past hesitation or grief.
explanation.es: Forma simple + 場合じゃない literalmente 'no es caso de X' = 'no es momento de X'. 泣いてる場合じゃない = 'no es momento de llorar'. Empuja a superar la duda.
explanation.pt-BR: Forma simples + 場合じゃない literalmente 'não é caso de X' = 'não é hora de X'. 泣いてる場合じゃない = 'não é hora de chorar'. Empurra para além da hesitação.

explanation.en: Plain form + さ at the end of a sentence is a casual, often masculine, assertive marker — 'you see / it is, you know'. ライバルになるのさ = 'you'll become a rival, you see'. Lighter than よ, more conversational than んだ.
explanation.es: Forma simple + さ al final es un marcador asertivo casual, típicamente masculino — 'sabes / es así'. ライバルになるのさ = 'te vas a volver un rival, sabes'. Más ligero que よ.
explanation.pt-BR: Forma simples + さ no fim da frase é marcador assertivo casual, geralmente masculino — 'sabe / é assim'. ライバルになるのさ = 'vai virar um rival, sabe'. Mais leve que よ.

grammar_points.name: 〜のは〜から (no wa ... kara) — the reason is because

explanation.en:
How it works:
The pattern Verb/Clause + のは (no wa) ... から (kara) is used to explain a reason. のは (no wa) nominalizes the first clause ("the fact that ..."), and から (kara) gives the reason. It is like saying "The reason [X] is because [Y]." This is a polite and clear way to give explanations.

Example from this song:
The song uses this structure to express why the singer feels driven to rewrite their story — the reason lies in past pain.

More examples:
• 遅れたのは電車が止まったからです (okureta no wa densha ga tomatta kara desu) — "the reason I was late is because the train stopped"
• 泣いているのは嬉しいからだ (naite iru no wa ureshii kara da) — "the reason I'm crying is because I'm happy"
• ここに来たのは君に会いたかったからだ (koko ni kita no wa kimi ni aitakatta kara da) — "the reason I came here is because I wanted to see you"

grammar_points.conjugation_path: Clause + のは (no wa) + Reason + から (kara) → "the reason ~ is because ~"

grammar_points.name: 〜はず (hazu) — supposed to / should be

explanation.en:
How it works:
The pattern Verb plain form + はず (hazu) expresses an expectation — something that should logically be true based on evidence or prior knowledge. はず (hazu) means "it is expected that ~" or "it should be ~." When reality does not match the expectation, it often pairs with なのに (nanoni, "but") to express surprise or frustration.

Example from this song:
The singer references expectations that did not match reality — things that were supposed to be true but were not.

More examples:
• もう届いたはずだ (mou todoita hazu da) — "it should have arrived by now"
• 彼は知っているはずだ (kare wa shitte iru hazu da) — "he should know (about it)"
• 簡単なはずだったのに (kantan na hazu datta noni) — "it was supposed to be easy, but..."

grammar_points.conjugation_path: Verb plain form + はず (hazu) → "should be / is expected to"

grammar_points.name: 〜られぬ (rarenu) — literary negative potential

explanation.en:
How it works:
The ending 〜られぬ (rarenu) is the classical Japanese form of the modern 〜られない (rarenai, "cannot"). The ぬ (nu) is the classical negative ending, equivalent to modern ない (nai). This form sounds old-fashioned and dramatic, making it popular in songs, poetry, and literary writing. It adds emotional weight and gravity.

Example from this song:
忘れられぬ (wasurerarenu) — "cannot forget" (literary)
A more powerful way to express inability to forget, as if the memory is eternally etched.

More examples:
• 信じられぬ (shinjirarenui) — "unbelievable" (literary)
• 許されぬ罪 (yurusarenu tsumi) — "an unforgivable sin"
• 逃れられぬ運命 (nogarerarenu unmei) — "an inescapable fate"

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 忘れる (wasureru, "to forget") → 忘れられる (wasurerareru, potential) → 忘れられぬ (wasurerarenu, literary negative, "cannot forget")

grammar_points.name: 複合動詞 (fukugou doushi) — compound verbs with 〜去る

explanation.en:
How it works:
Compound verbs combine two verbs to create a more specific meaning. The pattern Verb ます-stem (masu-stem) + 去る (saru, "to leave/remove") intensifies the base verb, adding the nuance of doing something completely or thoroughly. 消す (kesu, "to erase") + 去る (saru) = 消し去る (keshi saru, "to completely erase / wipe out").

Example from this song:
消し去る (keshi saru) — "to completely erase"
Not just erasing, but wiping out entirely without a trace.

More examples:
• 走り去る (hashiri saru) — "to run away / run off completely"
• 飛び去る (tobi saru) — "to fly away"
• 立ち去る (tachi saru) — "to leave / walk away"

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 消す (kesu, "to erase") → 消し (keshi, masu-stem) + 去る (saru, "to leave") → 消し去る (keshi saru, "to completely erase")

grammar_points.name: 命令形 〜くれ (kure) — give me! / do it for me!

explanation.en:
How it works:
くれ (kure) is the imperative (command) form of くれる (kureru, "to give/do for me"). It is a blunt, masculine demand — "give me ~!" or "do ~ for me!" Adding よ (yo) as くれよ (kure yo) softens it slightly with emphasis. This is rougher than ください (kudasai) and is common in anime dialogue and song lyrics.

Example from this song:
くれよ (kure yo) — "give it to me!" / "do it for me!"
The singer demands something with raw emotional urgency.

More examples:
• 教えてくれ (oshiete kure) — "tell me!" (blunt)
• 待ってくれ (matte kure) — "wait for me!"
• 黙ってくれ (damatte kure) — "shut up!" / "be quiet!"

grammar_points.conjugation_path: くれる (kureru, "to give/do for me") → くれ (kure, imperative) → くれよ (kure yo, emphatic imperative, "give me!")

grammar_points.name: 四字熟語 (yojijukugo) — four-character idioms

explanation.en:
How it works:
Four-character idioms (四字熟語, yojijukugo) are compact expressions made of four kanji, originally from classical Chinese. Each carries a deep meaning packed into just four characters. They are used in formal writing, speeches, and dramatic contexts like song lyrics. They sound powerful and intellectual.

Example from this song:
起死回生 (kishikaisei) — "snatching life from the jaws of death" / "a miraculous comeback"
全身全霊 (zenshinzenrei) — "with all one's body and soul" / "with everything you've got"

More examples:
• 一期一会 (ichigoichie) — "once in a lifetime encounter" — treasure every meeting
• 七転八起 (nanakorobi yaoki) — "fall seven times, get up eight" — never give up
• 自業自得 (jigou jitoku) — "you reap what you sow"

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 起死回生 (kishikaisei): 起 (ki, "rise") + 死 (shi, "death") + 回 (kai, "turn") + 生 (sei, "life") → "turn death into life"

explanation.en: Group-1 verbs swap final -u for -e (追いかける is Group-2, but compare 急ぐ → 急げ). Group-2 verbs add -ろ (入れる → 入れろ, 追いかける → 追いかけろ). Blunt and forceful — used in song lyrics, fight scenes; rude in everyday talk.
explanation.es: Grupo 1: -u → -e. Grupo 2: -る → -ろ (入れる → 入れろ, 追いかける → 追いかけろ). Orden directa — en letras, peleas; grosera en el día a día.
explanation.pt-BR: Grupo 1: -u → -e. Grupo 2: -る → -ろ (入れる → 入れろ, 追いかける → 追いかけろ). Comando direto — usado em letras, lutas; grosseiro no dia a dia.

grammar_points.name: Sentence-final ぜ / さ / ぞ (masculine emphatic particles)

explanation.en: Three closely related particles add masculine emphasis: ぜ (rough, urgent), さ (casual, conversational), ぞ (warning/declaration). 翔ぶのさ 'we soar, you see'; ハンパじゃないぜ 'no joke!'. Female speakers tend to avoid all three.
explanation.es: Tres partículas afines añaden énfasis masculino: ぜ (brusca, urgente), さ (casual), ぞ (aviso/declaración). 翔ぶのさ 'volamos, sabes'; ハンパじゃないぜ '¡no es ninguna broma!'. Las hablantes mujeres suelen evitarlas.
explanation.pt-BR: Três partículas próximas adicionam ênfase masculina: ぜ (rude, urgente), さ (casual, conversacional), ぞ (aviso/declaração). 翔ぶのさ 'nós voamos, sabe', ハンパじゃないぜ 'não é coisa pouca!'. Mulheres tendem a evitar.

grammar_points.name: Verb-stem + に + 行く/来る (go/come to do X)

explanation.en: Verb stem + に + a movement verb expresses purpose: 'go (or come) in order to X'. 見つけに行く 'go to find'; 食べに行く 'go to eat'; 遊びに来る 'come to hang out'. The motion and the goal are stated in one phrase.
explanation.es: Raíz del verbo + に + verbo de movimiento expresa propósito: 'ir (o venir) a hacer X'. 見つけに行く 'ir a encontrar'; 食べに行く 'ir a comer'; 遊びに来る 'venir a jugar'.
explanation.pt-BR: Radical do verbo + に + verbo de movimento expressa propósito: 'ir (ou vir) para fazer X'. 見つけに行く 'ir achar'; 食べに行く 'ir comer'; 遊びに来る 'vir brincar'.

explanation.en: Verb stem + は + しない is a strong, often defiant negation: 'won't (do that), no way'. かないはしない 'no enemy can stand a chance'; 捨てはしない 'I won't throw it away'. Stronger than plain 〜ない.
explanation.es: Raíz del verbo + は + しない es negación enfática, a menudo desafiante. かないはしない 'ningún enemigo está a la altura'; 捨てはしない 'no lo voy a tirar'. Más fuerte que 〜ない.
explanation.pt-BR: Radical do verbo + は + しない é negação enfática, frequentemente desafiadora. かないはしない 'nenhum inimigo é páreo'; 捨てはしない 'não vou jogar fora'. Mais forte que 〜ない.

grammar_points.name: Mimetic adverbs (ぎっしり, どっさり, キラキラ etc.)

explanation.en: Japanese has hundreds of mimetic words (giseigo/gitaigo) describing manner, sound, or feeling. ぎっしり 'packed densely'; どっさり 'in heaps'; キラキラ 'sparkling'; ワクワク 'excited heart-pounding'. Often inserted between phrases for vivid effect — sometimes Romanised in song lyrics for stylish look.
explanation.es: El japonés tiene cientos de palabras miméticas (giseigo/gitaigo). ぎっしり 'apretadamente lleno'; どっさり 'a montones'; キラキラ 'resplandeciente'; ワクワク 'corazón emocionado'. Se insertan para efecto vivo — a veces romanizadas en letras.
explanation.pt-BR: O japonês tem centenas de palavras miméticas (giseigo/gitaigo). ぎっしり 'denso, lotado'; どっさり 'aos montes'; キラキラ 'cintilante'; ワクワク 'coração acelerado'. Inseridas para efeito vivo — às vezes romanizadas em letras.

grammar_points.name: 〜ならきっと (nara kitto: if... then surely)

explanation.en:
How it works: Combine the conditional なら (nara, 'if') with the adverb きっと (kitto, 'surely') to express confident prediction: 'if X, then surely Y.'

Example from this song: 世界ならきっと (sekai nara kitto) = 'if it's this world, then surely...' — expressing confidence that this particular world can achieve something

More examples:
• 君ならきっとできる (kimi nara kitto dekiru, 'if it's you, you can surely do it') — encouragement
• 明日ならきっと会える (ashita nara kitto aeru, 'if it's tomorrow, we can surely meet')
• 努力するならきっと報われる (doryoku suru nara kitto mukuwareru, 'if you work hard, you'll surely be rewarded')

Note: きっと adds confidence to any statement. Combined with なら, it creates a powerful expression of faith: 'given this condition, I'm certain of the result.' Very common in encouraging and motivational contexts.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 世界 (sekai, 'world') + なら (nara, 'if') + きっと (kitto, 'surely') → 世界ならきっと (sekai nara kitto, 'if it's this world, then surely')

grammar_points.name: 〜てゆく (te yuku: to go on doing)

explanation.en:
How it works: てゆく (te yuku) is the literary/poetic form of ていく (te iku), expressing an action that continues moving into the future. ゆく (yuku) is the classical form of 行く (iku).

Example from this song: 彩ってゆく (irodotte yuku) = 'continues to color (into the future)' — from 彩る (irodoru, 'to color') → 彩って (irodotte) + ゆく (yuku)

More examples:
• 消えてゆく (kiete yuku, 'fading away') — from 消える (kieru, 'to disappear')
• 変わってゆく (kawatte yuku, 'gradually changing') — from 変わる (kawaru, 'to change')
• 歩いてゆく (aruite yuku, 'walking onward') — from 歩く (aruku, 'to walk')

Note: てゆく and ていく mean the same thing, but てゆく has a more poetic, emotional, or literary feel. Songs and literature strongly prefer ゆく over いく for its elegance.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 彩る (irodoru, 'to color') → 彩って (irodotte) + ゆく (yuku, 'to go on') → 彩ってゆく (irodotte yuku, 'goes on coloring')

grammar_points.name: 〜ば (ba: if; when)

explanation.en:
How it works: The ば (ba) conditional means 'if' or 'when.' For godan verbs, change the final -u to -e and add ば. For ichidan verbs, drop る and add れば.

Example from this song: 合えば (aeba) = 'if we come together' — from 合う (au, 'to match/come together') → 合え (ae) + ば (ba)

More examples:
• 行けば (ikeba, 'if you go') — from 行く (iku, 'to go')
• 見れば (mireba, 'if you see') — from 見る (miru, 'to see')
• 良ければ (yokereba, 'if it's good / if you don't mind') — from 良い (yoi, 'good')

Note: ば implies a natural consequence: 'if A, then B naturally follows.' 合う → 合えば follows the standard godan pattern: u → e + ば.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 合う (au, 'to come together') → 合えば (aeba, 'if we come together')

grammar_points.name: 〜ず (zu: without doing)

explanation.en:
How it works: ず (zu) is the classical negative form meaning 'without doing.' It replaces ない in literary or formal contexts. For most verbs, change the ない-form's ない to ず.

Example from this song: 変わらず (kawarazu) = 'without changing / unchangingly' — from 変わる (kawaru, 'to change') → 変わらない (kawaranai) → 変わらず (kawarazu)

More examples:
• 言わず (iwazu, 'without saying') — from 言う (iu, 'to say')
• 食べず (tabezu, 'without eating') — from 食べる (taberu, 'to eat')
• 諦めず (akiramezu, 'without giving up') — from 諦める (akirameru, 'to give up')

Note: ず is the literary equivalent of ないで or なくて. Exception: する → せず (sezu), not しず. ず can be followed by に to connect: 食べずに寝た (tabezu ni neta, 'slept without eating').

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 変わる (kawaru, 'to change') → 変わらない (kawaranai, 'doesn't change') → 変わらず (kawarazu, 'without changing')

grammar_points.name: 〜てくれる (te kureru: to do for me)

explanation.en:
How it works: Attach くれる (kureru) to a verb's te-form to express that someone does something for the speaker's benefit. It conveys gratitude.

Example from this song: 君がくれたもの (kimi ga kureta mono) = 'the things you gave me' — from くれる (kureru, 'to give to me') → くれた (kureta, past) + もの (mono, 'things')

More examples:
• 笑ってくれた (waratte kureta, 'smiled for me') — from 笑う (warau, 'to smile')
• 来てくれてうれしい (kite kurete ureshii, 'happy that you came for me')
• 待っていてくれた (matte ite kureta, 'was waiting for me') — from 待つ (matsu, 'to wait')

Note: くれる is essential in Japanese — it marks that an action benefited the speaker. Without it, the sentence is neutral. With it, there's warmth and gratitude. Very common in love songs.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 君 (kimi, 'you') + が (ga) + くれた (kureta, 'gave me') + もの (mono, 'things') → 君がくれたもの (kimi ga kureta mono, 'the things you gave me')

grammar_points.name: 〜たい (tai: want to do)

explanation.en:
How it works: Take the verb stem (masu-stem) and add たい (tai) to express wanting to do something. This is one of the first and most important grammar patterns for beginners.

Example from this song: 帰りたい (kaeritai) = 'want to return' — from 帰る (kaeru, 'to return') → 帰り (kaeri, stem) + たい (tai, 'want to'). Also: 育てたい (sodatetai) = 'want to raise' and 語りたい (kataritai) = 'want to talk about'

More examples:
• 食べる (taberu, 'to eat') → 食べたい (tabetai, 'want to eat')
• 行く (iku, 'to go') → 行きたい (ikitai, 'want to go')
• 見る (miru, 'to see') → 見たい (mitai, 'want to see')

Note: For -ru verbs (ichidan), drop る and add たい. For -u verbs (godan), change the last syllable to its い-row equivalent and add たい: く→きたい, む→みたい, す→したい. たい conjugates like an い-adjective: たくない (don't want), たかった (wanted).

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 帰る (kaeru, 'to return') → 帰り (kaeri, stem) + たい (tai, 'want to') → 帰りたい (kaeritai, 'want to return') / 育てる (sodateru, 'to raise') → 育てたい (sodatetai, 'want to raise')

grammar_points.name: 〜のなら (no nara: if it is that)

explanation.en:
How it works: Add のなら (no nara) after a verb to express a conditional that assumes the situation — 'if it is the case that X' or 'given that X'.

Example from this song: くるのなら (kuru no nara) = 'if (that time) comes' — from くる (kuru, 'to come') + のなら (no nara, 'if it is that')

More examples:
• 行く (iku, 'to go') → 行くのなら (iku no nara, 'if you're going')
• 諦める (akirameru, 'to give up') → 諦めるのなら (akirameru no nara, 'if you're going to give up')
• 会える (aeru, 'can meet') → 会えるのなら (aeru no nara, 'if we can meet')

Note: のなら assumes the condition has been stated or is likely. It often implies 'since you've decided...' or 'well, if that's the case...' It's more emphatic than plain なら.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: くる (kuru, 'to come') + のなら (no nara, 'if it is that') → くるのなら (kuru no nara, 'if it comes')

grammar_points.name: 〜だらけ (darake: full of)

explanation.en:
How it works: Attach だらけ (darake) after a noun to mean 'full of' or 'riddled with', usually with a negative or overwhelming connotation.

Example from this song: 強がりだらけ (tsuyogari darake) = 'full of bravado / nothing but false bravery' — from 強がり (tsuyogari, 'bravado/putting on a brave front') + だらけ (darake, 'full of')

More examples:
• 嘘 (uso, 'lies') → 嘘だらけ (uso darake, 'full of lies')
• 傷 (kizu, 'wounds') → 傷だらけ (kizu darake, 'covered in wounds')
• 失敗 (shippai, 'failure') → 失敗だらけ (shippai darake, 'full of failures')

Note: だらけ almost always carries a negative nuance — being overwhelmed by something undesirable. To modify a noun: だらけの + noun: 傷だらけの体 (kizu darake no karada, 'a body covered in wounds').

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 強がり (tsuyogari, 'bravado') + だらけ (darake, 'full of') → 強がりだらけ (tsuyogari darake, 'full of bravado')

grammar_points.name: 〜でいい (de ii: it's fine with)

explanation.en:
How it works: Use noun + でいい (de ii) to express that something is acceptable or sufficient — 'X is fine' or 'X will do'. It can also imply settling for something.

Example from this song: 夢物語でいいから (monogatari de ii kara) = 'even if it's just a fairy tale, that's fine' — from 夢物語 (yumemonogatari, 'fairy tale') + でいい (de ii, 'is fine') + から (kara, 'because/so')

More examples:
• 水 (mizu, 'water') → 水でいい (mizu de ii, 'water is fine')
• 明日 (ashita, 'tomorrow') → 明日でいい (ashita de ii, 'tomorrow is fine')
• これ (kore, 'this') → これでいい (kore de ii, 'this is fine')

Note: でいい can sometimes sound like 'settling' — 水でいい means 'water is fine (I don't need anything special)'. For 'water is good/what I want', use がいい: 水がいい. The difference is subtle but important.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 夢物語 (yumemonogatari, 'fairy tale') + でいい (de ii, 'is fine') + から (kara, 'so') → 夢物語でいいから (yumemonogatari de ii kara, 'a fairy tale is fine')

grammar_points.name: 意志形 + よ (volitional + yo: let's)

explanation.en:
How it works: Use the volitional form (〜よう/〜おう) and add よ (yo) for a casual, warm invitation — 'let's do X!' The よ adds encouragement.

Example from this song: 帰ろうよ (kaerouyo) = 'let's go home!' — from 帰る (kaeru, 'to return') → 帰ろう (kaerou, volitional) + よ (yo, encouragement)

More examples:
• 食べる (taberu, 'to eat') → 食べようよ (tabeyou yo, 'let's eat!')
• 行く (iku, 'to go') → 行こうよ (ikou yo, 'let's go!')
• 遊ぶ (asobu, 'to play') → 遊ぼうよ (asobou yo, 'let's play!')

Note: The volitional alone (行こう) is a suggestion; adding よ makes it more encouraging and friendly. For godan verbs: change final syllable to お-row + う. For ichidan verbs: drop る, add よう. する→しよう, 来る→来よう (koyou).

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 帰る (kaeru, 'to return') → 帰ろう (kaerou, volitional) + よ (yo, encouragement) → 帰ろうよ (kaerouyo, 'let's go home!')

grammar_points.name: 〜てた (teta: had been doing)

explanation.en:
How it works: Use てた (teta), the casual contraction of ていた (te ita), to express past progressive — 'was doing X' or 'had been doing X'.

Example from this song: 探してた (sagashiteta) = 'had been searching' — from 探す (sagasu, 'to search') → 探していた (sagashite ita, 'was searching') → 探してた (sagashiteta, casual). Also: 気付いてた (kizuiteta) = 'had noticed'

More examples:
• 待つ (matsu, 'to wait') → 待ってた (matteta, 'had been waiting')
• 考える (kangaeru, 'to think') → 考えてた (kangaeteta, 'had been thinking')
• 知る (shiru, 'to know') → 知ってた (shitteta, 'had known')

Note: The contraction pattern: ている → てる (present), ていた → てた (past), ていない → てない (negative). Understanding these casual contractions is essential for comprehending songs and everyday Japanese.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 探す (sagasu, 'to search') → 探していた (sagashite ita, 'was searching') → 探してた (sagashiteta, 'had been searching' — casual)

meaning.en: looks like (I) might be able to fully change

translations.en: Like I could change myself — even the whole world
translations.es: Como si pudiera cambiarme a mí mismo — y al mundo entero
translations.pt-BR: Como se eu pudesse mudar a mim mesmo — até o mundo

literal_meaning.en: Self (object) world even-also, change-completely-can-seemingly

cultural_context.en: Stacking 〜さえ + も is emphatic: '(not just X but) even Y too'. 自分を…世界さえも = 'myself, and even the world'. The grand scale matches Code Geass's themes of remaking reality.

translations.en: That moment is always right next to me...
translations.es: Ese instante siempre está justo a mi lado...
translations.pt-BR: Esse instante sempre está bem ao meu lado...

literal_meaning.en: Moment (topic) always right beside at

translations.en: Staring down the frustration I can't hide, and the self that stands rooted
translations.es: Mirando de frente la irritación que no logro ocultar y al yo que se queda paralizado
translations.pt-BR: Encarando a irritação que não consigo esconder e o eu que ficou paralisado

literal_meaning.en: Cannot-hide frustration and stand-frozen self (object) gazing

cultural_context.en: 〜ぬ is the classical/literary negative ending (= 〜ない): 隠せぬ = 隠せない. Common in lyrics, idioms, and proverbs. Sounds heavier and more poetic than the modern form.

translations.en: While wavering, while agonizing
translations.es: Mientras dudas, mientras te atormentas
translations.pt-BR: Hesitando, sofrendo

literal_meaning.en: Wavering-while, agonizing-while

translations.en: While regretting too — it's fine, just decide
translations.es: Aun arrepintiéndote — está bien, solo decide
translations.pt-BR: Se arrependendo também — tudo bem, é só decidir

literal_meaning.en: Regretting-while, if-decide good (assertion)

cultural_context.en: 〜ばいい ('it's fine if you do X') is gentle permission/encouragement: 'just go ahead and decide'. Adding さ softens it further into a reassuring 'you'll be alright if you do'.

translations.en: A single word you gave me — and the confusion vanished
translations.es: Una sola palabra que me diste — y la confusión se esfumó
translations.pt-BR: Uma palavra que você me deu — e a confusão se foi

literal_meaning.en: You (subject) gave word one, hesitation (topic) vanish-away

cultural_context.en: くれる is the giving verb that marks the giver as benefitting the speaker — 'you gave (to me)'. Different from あげる (you give to someone else) or もらう (I receive).

translations.en: Light streamed into my once-empty room
translations.es: La luz entró en mi cuarto, antes vacío
translations.pt-BR: A luz invadiu meu quarto antes vazio

literal_meaning.en: Empty was, my room into, light (subject) shone

cultural_context.en: 光が射す ('light shines/streams in') is a stock phrase for sunlight reaching a previously dark place. Often metaphorical for hope arriving.

translations.en: The wide sky I looked up at clears more and more, deeply blue
translations.es: El gran cielo que miré se va aclarando, completamente azul
translations.pt-BR: O céu amplo que eu olhei vai ficando azul, totalmente limpo

literal_meaning.en: Looked-up sky (subject) bluely, become-completely-clear-and go

cultural_context.en: 澄む = 'to be clear/limpid'; + 切る ('all the way') = 澄み切る ('become totally clear'); + 〜ていく ('go on doing') = 'progressively becoming clearer'. Three layers stacking the same image.

translations.en: I decided to open the window I'd shut tight
translations.es: Decidí abrir la ventana que había cerrado
translations.pt-BR: Decidi abrir a janela que eu havia trancado

literal_meaning.en: Sealed window (object) open thing (object) decided

cultural_context.en: 閉ざす ('to seal, shut tight') is a heavier, more permanent shutting than 閉める. Pairs with 心を閉ざす ('to close one's heart'). Opening it is metaphorical for committing to change.

translations.en: Searching for an answer that should exist in this unfulfilled daily life
translations.es: Buscando una respuesta que debería existir en este día a día insatisfecho
translations.pt-BR: Procurando uma resposta que deveria existir neste cotidiano incompleto

literal_meaning.en: Cannot-be-filled daily-life in, exist-should answer (object) searching

translations.en: Alone in the morning sun — when I turn toward a gentle voice
translations.es: Solo bajo el sol de la mañana — cuando me giro hacia una voz suave
translations.pt-BR: Sozinho no sol da manhã — quando me viro para uma voz suave

literal_meaning.en: Morning-sun in alone, soft voice toward, if-turn

translations.en: Inside that dazzling sunlight — you smile, just like that
translations.es: En medio de esa luz cegadora — tú sonríes, sin más
translations.pt-BR: No meio daquela luz ofuscante — você sorri, sem mais

literal_meaning.en: Dazzling sunlight's midst, casually you (subject) smile

cultural_context.en: ふと is a beautifully untranslatable adverb — 'unexpectedly / casually / out of nowhere'. ふと君が微笑む = 'you smiled, unbidden, the way someone does without thinking'.

translations.en: The sealed window is about to open
translations.es: La ventana cerrada está a punto de abrirse
translations.pt-BR: A janela trancada está prestes a se abrir

literal_meaning.en: Sealed window (subject) likely-to-open become

cultural_context.en: Verb stem + そう ('looks like / seems about to') + になる = 'comes to look like it will'. Common pattern: 泣きそうになる ('feel like I might cry'), 倒れそうになる ('feel like I might collapse').

translations.en: That presence is right before my eyes...
translations.es: Esa presencia está justo delante de mí...
translations.pt-BR: Essa presença está bem na minha frente...

literal_meaning.en: Existence (topic) my eye's-front at

translations.en: I feel that moment — right here, right now...
translations.es: Siento ese instante — aquí y ahora...
translations.pt-BR: Sinto esse instante — agora, aqui mesmo...

literal_meaning.en: Moment (object) feel, now here at

translations.en: Stretching out both hands toward the light...
translations.es: Tendiendo las dos manos hacia la luz...
translations.pt-BR: Estendendo as duas mãos rumo à luz...

literal_meaning.en: Light toward, both-hands (object) stretching

cultural_context.en: へと is the directional particle へ ('toward') + と (an emphatic/quoting marker) — slightly heavier than へ alone, common in lyrics for added gravity.

translations.en: The colors of the sky and a fragrant wind, blowing right through my heart
translations.es: Los colores del cielo y un viento perfumado que cruza mi corazón
translations.pt-BR: As cores do céu e um vento perfumado que atravessam meu coração

literal_meaning.en: Heart (path) blow-through, sky's color, fragrant wind

cultural_context.en: 心を吹き抜ける ('to blow right through one's heart') is a stock J-rock image: a sensation so strong it passes through you like wind. Pairing it with the song's title (色/colors) closes the lyric on an open, sensory note.

explanation.en: 〜さえ marks something extreme as 'even X'. Adding も intensifies it: 世界さえも = 'even the world (no less)'. Often paired with conditional or volitional clauses to set up a 'if even X, then surely Y' frame.
explanation.es: 〜さえ marca algo extremo como 'hasta X / incluso X'. Añadir も lo intensifica: 世界さえも = 'incluso el propio mundo'. Suele acompañar a condicionales: 'si hasta X, seguro que Y'.
explanation.pt-BR: 〜さえ marca algo extremo como 'até X'. Adicionar も intensifica: 世界さえも = 'até o próprio mundo'. Costuma combinar com condicionais para 'se até X, então com certeza Y'.

grammar_points.name: Verb-て + しまえそう ('looks like one might be able to fully do')

explanation.en: Three layers: 〜てしまう ('do completely / end up doing') + 〜える (potential 'be able to') + 〜そう ('looks like'). 変えてしまえそう = 'looks like (I) could fully change (it)'. Used to express a sudden sense of possibility for a big, irreversible act.
explanation.es: Tres capas: 〜てしまう ('hacer del todo') + 〜える (potencial 'poder') + 〜そう ('parece'). 変えてしまえそう = 'parece que podría cambiarlo del todo'. Sensación repentina de poder con algo grande.
explanation.pt-BR: Três camadas: 〜てしまう ('fazer por completo') + 〜える (potencial 'poder') + 〜そう ('parece'). 変えてしまえそう = 'parece que eu conseguiria mudar por completo'. Sensação repentina de poder fazer algo grande.

explanation.en: 〜ぬ is the classical negative ending equivalent to 〜ない: 隠せぬ = 隠せない ('cannot hide'), 満たせぬ = 満たせない ('cannot be filled'). Common in lyrics, set phrases (時の流れに身をまかせぬ), and proverbs. Reads as more solemn or old-fashioned.
explanation.es: 〜ぬ es la terminación negativa clásica equivalente a 〜ない: 隠せぬ = 隠せない, 満たせぬ = 満たせない. Frecuente en letras, frases hechas y proverbios. Suena más solemne/antiguo.
explanation.pt-BR: 〜ぬ é a terminação negativa clássica equivalente a 〜ない: 隠せぬ = 隠せない, 満たせぬ = 満たせない. Comum em letras, expressões fixas e provérbios. Soa mais solene/antigo.

explanation.en: Verb stem + ながら expresses two simultaneous actions by the same subject: 迷いながら 悩みながら 悔やみながら ('while wavering, while worrying, while regretting'). Stacking ながら-clauses is a common rhythmic device in lyrics — accumulates a list of overlapping internal states.
explanation.es: Raíz verbal + ながら expresa dos acciones simultáneas del mismo sujeto: 迷いながら 悩みながら 悔やみながら. Apilar varios ながら es un recurso rítmico en letras — acumula estados internos solapados.
explanation.pt-BR: Raiz verbal + ながら exprime duas ações simultâneas do mesmo sujeito: 迷いながら 悩みながら 悔やみながら. Empilhar ながら é um recurso rítmico em letras — junta estados emocionais sobrepostos.

grammar_points.name: 〜ばいい (it's fine if you / just do X)

explanation.en: Conditional 〜ば + いい literally 'if X then it's good' = 'just do X / it'll be fine to do X'. Gentle permission or encouragement: 決めればいい ('it's fine to just decide'). Adding さ at the end softens it further into reassurance.
explanation.es: Condicional 〜ば + いい significa 'si X, entonces bien' = 'basta con hacer X / hazlo y ya'. Permiso/aliento suave: 決めればいい. Con さ al final suena aún más reconfortante.
explanation.pt-BR: Condicional 〜ば + いい significa 'se X, então tudo bem' = 'é só fazer X / pode fazer X'. Permissão ou incentivo suave: 決めればいい. Com さ no fim, vira tom mais reconfortante.

explanation.en: Verb stem + 切る ('to do completely'): 澄み切る ('become totally clear'). Verb stem + 抜ける ('to pass through completely'): 駆け抜ける ('race through'), 吹き抜ける ('blow through'). Verb stem + 去る ('to depart'): 消え去る ('vanish completely'). Each suffix adds a flavor of completeness or directional motion.
explanation.es: Raíz verbal + 切る ('hacer del todo'): 澄み切る. Raíz + 抜ける ('atravesar'): 駆け抜ける, 吹き抜ける. Raíz + 去る ('marcharse'): 消え去る. Cada sufijo aporta un matiz de totalidad o movimiento direccional.
explanation.pt-BR: Raiz verbal + 切る ('fazer por completo'): 澄み切る. Raiz + 抜ける ('atravessar'): 駆け抜ける, 吹き抜ける. Raiz + 去る ('partir'): 消え去る. Cada sufixo dá um sabor de totalidade ou movimento direcional.

grammar_points.name: Verb stem + そう (looks like / seems about to)

explanation.en: Verb stem + そう = 'looks like X is about to happen / seems likely to'. 開きそう ('looks like it'll open'); 泣きそう ('about to cry'); 倒れそう ('about to fall'). Adding になる ('come to be that') makes it 'come to be on the verge of': 開きそうになる.
explanation.es: Raíz verbal + そう = 'parece a punto de / parece que va a'. 開きそう, 泣きそう, 倒れそう. Añadir になる = 'estar a punto de': 開きそうになる.
explanation.pt-BR: Raiz verbal + そう = 'parece prestes a / parece que vai'. 開きそう, 泣きそう, 倒れそう. Adicionar になる = 'estar prestes a': 開きそうになる.

translations.en: I pressed my ear tight against your back and held you — this body of mine, like a borderline, just gets in the way; it feels like it could drift off somewhere.
translations.es: Apreté el oído contra tu espalda y te abracé — este cuerpo mío, como una línea divisoria, sólo estorba; siento que podría irse a algún lado.
translations.pt-BR: Encostei meu ouvido bem junto às suas costas e te abracei — esse meu corpo, que parece uma linha de fronteira, só atrapalha; tenho a impressão de que pode escapar para algum canto.

literal_meaning.en: 'To-back ear snugly-pressing, embraced. Boundary-line-like body is hindrance, right? Somewhere-going-seems-like, (emphasis).' The narrator imagines her skin as a border that keeps her and the beloved apart.

cultural_context.en: ぴっと is a mimetic (giongo) adverb evoking a tight snap-fit — Japanese pop lyrics use mimetics like this to convey physical sensation without medical vocabulary.

translations.en: Because if I stay quiet, this feeling feels like it'll tear apart — in a world only three meters across, I want to cling to you more, closer still.
translations.es: Porque si me quedo callada, este sentimiento parece a punto de desgarrarse — en un mundo de apenas tres metros a la redonda, quiero pegarme más a ti.
translations.pt-BR: Porque se eu ficar calada, esse sentimento parece que vai se rasgar — num mundo de apenas três metros de raio, quero grudar em você cada vez mais.

literal_meaning.en: 'Staying-silent if, about-to-tear-apart because, this-kind-of feeling. Radius 3-meter within-of world in, more more, want-to-cling (emphasis).'

translations.en: Taking turns pedaling, we pass the drooping sunflowers on the street, swallowing up the wind as we go — feels like we could just lift off. The first time I felt your body heat, I wanted to be stronger than anyone — a warm rhythm, our two hearts drawing together.
translations.es: Turnándonos en los pedales, dejamos atrás la calle de los girasoles caídos, tragándonos el viento — parece que hasta podríamos volar. La primera vez que sentí tu calor corporal, quise ser más fuerte que nadie — un ritmo cálido, nuestros dos corazones uniéndose.
translations.pt-BR: Pedalando alternado, passamos pela rua dos girassóis caídos, engolindo o vento — parece que a gente até voaria. Na primeira vez que senti seu calor, quis ser mais forte que qualquer um — um ritmo quente, nossos dois corações se grudando.

literal_meaning.en: 'Taking-turns with pedal pedaling, bow-of-sunflower passing, rapidly wind swallowing — like-that could-fly, right? For-the-first-time felt your body-heat. Than-anyone stronger want-to-become. Warm rhythm. Two-hearts are drawing-together.'

cultural_context.en: おじぎのひまわり ('bowing sunflower') is a poetic image — a sunflower whose heavy head has drooped into a bow, like the Japanese おじぎ greeting. 2コ is a colloquial written form of 二個 mixing digits and katakana.

meaning.en: drawing together (colloquial くっついていく)

translations.en: Lip to lip, eye to eye, hand to hand — God hasn't forbidden a thing. I love you. I love you. I love you. I'm not chastened yet; grown-ups just don't get it. It hurts, it aches, I want to show you — I'll burst. I'm waiting while I look the other way, so with my hesitating hand still in my pocket, touch my cheek — cast a spell on this power called love.
translations.es: Labio con labio, ojo con ojo, mano con mano — Dios no ha prohibido nada. Te amo. Te amo. Te amo. Todavía no aprendo la lección; los adultos no lo entienden. Duele, aprieta, quiero mostrártelo — voy a estallar. Espero mirando hacia otro lado, así que con mi mano indecisa en el bolsillo, toca mi mejilla — lánzale un hechizo a esta fuerza que se llama amor.
translations.pt-BR: Lábio no lábio, olho no olho, mão na mão — Deus não proibiu coisa nenhuma. Eu te amo. Eu te amo. Eu te amo. Ainda não aprendi a lição; adulto não entende. Dói, aperta, quero mostrar — vou explodir. Estou esperando olhando pro outro lado, então com minha mão hesitante no bolso, toca minha bochecha — lança um feitiço nessa força chamada amor.

literal_meaning.en: 'Lip and lip, pupil and pupil and hand and hand. God anything at-all prohibition such-as isn't-doing. Loving. Loving. Loving. I still not-chastened, adult-as don't-understand. Painful, heartrending, wanting-to-show, I'll-burst. Other-way looking waiting because, pocket's hesitating hand with, cheek touching — in-love power on magic cast.'

cultural_context.en: そっぽを見る ('look the other way') is the classic Japanese shoujo gesture of shy affection — pretending not to watch while actually waiting. パンクしちゃう uses パンク (originally 'puncture/flat tire') as slang for emotional overload.

meaning.en: not chastened; not learned the lesson
don't get it (casual わからない)
pocket (cute form of ポケット)

translations.en: The way home — always taking the long route together. Under a sky that looks like spilled orange, I feel somehow HAPPY & SAD.
translations.es: El camino a casa — siempre dábamos el rodeo más largo juntos. Bajo un cielo como naranja derramado, de algún modo me siento HAPPY & SAD.
translations.pt-BR: O caminho pra casa — sempre dávamos a volta mais longa juntos. Sob um céu parecendo laranja derramado, de alguma forma me sinto HAPPY & SAD.

literal_meaning.en: 'Always together-(adv) long-way were-doing homeward-road. Orange spill-like sky in, somehow HAPPY & SAD.'

translations.en: Why were we born at all? We're each half, right? I try puzzling it out alone, but I just end up bad at it.
translations.es: ¿Por qué nacimos? Cada una es una mitad, ¿no? Lo pienso sola, pero al final se me da fatal.
translations.pt-BR: Por que a gente nasceu, afinal? Cada um é metade, né? Tento pensar sozinha, mas no fim das contas sou ruim nisso mesmo.

literal_meaning.en: 'We-(topic) why were-born? Half are right? Alone-by thinking-try but, after-all not-good-at-it (emphasis).' The song's title 1/2 surfaces here: each person is a half, completed by the other.

cultural_context.en: 半分だよね ('we're each a half, right?') is the thematic pivot — the song's title '1/2' comes from this idea of each person being half of a pair. へたっぴ is cute/childish slang from 下手 with the -っぴ diminutive suffix.

meaning.en: no good at it (cute form of 下手)

translations.en: A shoulder strong enough to hurl a ball so far it vanishes — I envied that, I wanted to be a boy. Soft as clear water, stronger than anyone — the way I was when I was little. Weird, isn't it — my tears are spilling over.
translations.es: Un hombro fuerte capaz de lanzar la pelota hasta que desaparece — lo envidiaba, quería ser niño. Suave como agua clara, más fuerte que nadie — como cuando era pequeña. Qué raro, ¿no? — las lágrimas se me caen.
translations.pt-BR: Um ombro forte o bastante pra jogar a bola tão longe que some — eu invejava isso, queria ser menino. Macia como água clara, mais forte que qualquer um — como eu era quando criança. Estranho, né — minhas lágrimas estão transbordando.

literal_meaning.en: 'Becoming-invisible to-extent far to ball can-throw strong shoulder — enviable, boy want-to-become. Clear water like softly, than-anyone want-to-be-stronger. Tiny-time like. Strange right, tear spilling-goes.'

cultural_context.en: おとこの子になりたかった ('I wanted to be a boy') is a nostalgic childhood memory — Japanese female pop lyrics of the era often revisited tomboy-phase regret as shorthand for losing a simpler strength.

meaning.en: spilling over (colloquial こぼれていく)
even if I'm told (passive + ても)

translations.en: We feel the same things the same way. Even if they tell me I can't reach, I want to jump, just like this. I'll give you a goodbye kiss — so hold that last-step distance tight, so the sun will never set.
translations.es: Sentimos lo mismo de la misma forma. Aunque me digan que no llegaré, quiero saltar tal cual. Te daré un beso de despedida — así que aprieta fuerte esa distancia del último paso, para que el sol nunca se ponga.
translations.pt-BR: A gente sente as mesmas coisas do mesmo jeito. Mesmo que me digam que não vou alcançar, quero pular assim mesmo. Vou te dar um beijo de despedida — então me abrace forte, nessa distância do último passo, pra que o sol nunca se ponha.

literal_meaning.en: 'Same thing same way-of-feeling doing. Won't-reach even-if-told, just-like-this want-to-jump. Bye-bye-of-kiss do because, last-step-of distance tightly hold. Sun forever doesn't-set so-that.'

translations.en: We watched one lonely sunset together, just the two of us. It's beautiful but... somehow I can't put it into words — somehow something's missing. Ba-bang-bang!
translations.es: Vimos juntos una puesta de sol solitaria, sólo nosotros dos. Es hermoso, pero... de algún modo no puedo decirlo — falta algo. ¡Ba-bang-bang!
translations.pt-BR: A gente ficou olhando um pôr do sol solitário, só nós dois. É bonito, mas... de alguma forma não consigo dizer — tem alguma coisa faltando. Ba-bang-bang!

literal_meaning.en: 'One-(piece)-of setting-sun solitarily, two-people with, were-watching. Beautiful but-(emphasis). Somehow can't-say right? Somehow isn't-enough (emphasis). Ba-bang-bang!'

cultural_context.en: ぽつんと is a mimetic adverb conveying a single, lonely dot in wide space — here it paints the sunset as an isolated spot of light. ババンバン! is a playful sound-effect closer, mimicking a drum or firework burst.

translations.en: Just as Nostradamus foretold, on the day this planet explodes — I want to be one with you. A warm rhythm, our two hearts drawing closer still.

literal_meaning.en: 'Nostradamus prophesied just-as, this planet explode day (topic), one-into want-to-become.' A 1997-era reference to the Nostradamus 1999 apocalypse prophecy — popular Japanese pop-culture touchstone at the time.

cultural_context.en: ノストラダムスの大予言 (Nostradamus's Great Prophecy) was a massive Japanese pop-culture phenomenon from the 1970s through the late 1990s, predicting Earth's destruction in July 1999. For a 1997 song, referencing it is a shorthand for 'right before the end of the world'.

grammar_points.name: 〜みたい (mitai — 'like/similar to')

explanation.en: Attached to nouns or plain-form verbs, 〜みたい expresses similarity or resemblance ('like X'). More casual than the bookish 〜のよう. In 境界線みたいな身体, みたい acts as a na-adjective modifying 身体.
explanation.es: Unido a sustantivos o verbos en forma simple, 〜みたい expresa semejanza ('como X'). Más coloquial que 〜のよう. En 境界線みたいな身体, funciona como adjetivo-na modificando 身体.
explanation.pt-BR: Ligado a substantivos ou verbos na forma simples, 〜みたい expressa semelhança ('como X'). Mais coloquial que 〜のよう. Em 境界線みたいな身体, funciona como adjetivo-na modificando 身体.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: noun / plain verb → + みたい → + な (before noun) / + に (before verb)

grammar_points.name: 〜そう (sou — 'looks like / seems about to')

explanation.en: Attached to a verb stem, 〜そう means the action looks about to happen: 飛べそう ('looks like [we] could fly'), ちぎれそう ('about to be torn'), いっちゃいそう ('looks about to go off'). The song uses this pattern five+ times to convey imminence.
explanation.es: Unido a la raíz del verbo, 〜そう expresa 'parece a punto de': 飛べそう ('parece que volaríamos'), ちぎれそう ('a punto de romperse'). La canción usa este patrón varias veces para sugerir inminencia.
explanation.pt-BR: Ligado ao radical verbal, 〜そう indica que algo 'parece prestes a acontecer': 飛べそう ('parece que vai voar'), ちぎれそう ('quase rasgando'). A música usa esse padrão várias vezes para evocar iminência.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: verb stem → + そう (e.g. 飛ぶ → 飛び → 飛べそう with potential stem)

grammar_points.name: 〜たい (tai — 'want to')

explanation.en: Attached to verb stem to express the speaker's desire: なりたい ('want to become'), ひっついてたい ('want to keep clinging'), ジャンプしたい ('want to jump'). Conjugates like an i-adjective (なりたかった = past).
explanation.es: Unido a la raíz verbal para expresar deseo propio: なりたい ('quiero llegar a ser'), ひっついてたい ('quiero seguir pegada'). Se conjuga como adjetivo-i (なりたかった = pasado).
explanation.pt-BR: Ligado ao radical verbal para expressar desejo próprio: なりたい ('quero me tornar'), ひっついてたい ('quero continuar grudada'). Conjuga-se como adjetivo-i (なりたかった = passado).

grammar_points.conjugation_path: dictionary form → ます-stem → + たい (e.g. なる → なり → なりたい)

grammar_points.name: 〜てない / 〜てる (colloquial shortening of 〜ていない / 〜ている)

explanation.en: In casual speech the い of 〜ている / 〜ていない is dropped: 待ってる (= 待っている), 懲りてない (= 懲りていない), してない (= していない), 黙ってる (= 黙っている). Used throughout the song to keep the tone conversational.
explanation.es: En el habla coloquial el い de 〜ている/〜ていない se elide: 待ってる, 懲りてない, 黙ってる. La canción lo usa en toda la letra para mantener un tono conversacional.
explanation.pt-BR: Na fala coloquial, o い de 〜ている/〜ていない cai: 待ってる (= 待っている), 懲りてない (= 懲りていない). A música usa esse encurtamento o tempo todo para manter o tom de conversa.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 待っている → 待ってる (drops い); 待っていない → 待ってない

grammar_points.name: 〜ように (you ni — 'so that / in order that')

explanation.en: After a negative verb, 〜ように expresses a wish or hope for something NOT to happen: 太陽がずっとしずまないように ('so that the sun will never set'). Also appears as 水のように ('like water') to mean 'in the manner of'.
explanation.es: Tras verbo negativo, 〜ように expresa deseo para que algo NO suceda: 太陽がずっとしずまないように ('para que el sol nunca se ponga'). También aparece como 水のように ('como agua').
explanation.pt-BR: Após verbo negativo, 〜ように expressa desejo para que algo NÃO aconteça: 太陽がずっとしずまないように ('para que o sol nunca se ponha'). Também aparece como 水のように ('como água').

grammar_points.conjugation_path: verb plain negative + ように (e.g. しずむ → しずまない → しずまないように)

grammar_points.name: 〜ても / 〜たって (te mo / tatte — 'even if')

explanation.en: The verb te-form + も grants a concessive meaning ('even if X'): 考えてもみる ('even if I try thinking'). The colloquial equivalent is 〜たって: 届かないって言われたって ('even if I'm told [it] won't reach'). Common in casual speech and lyrics.
explanation.es: Forma-te del verbo + も da sentido concesivo ('aunque X'): 考えてもみる. El equivalente coloquial es 〜たって: 届かないって言われたって ('aunque me digan que no llega').
explanation.pt-BR: Forma-te do verbo + も cria sentido concessivo ('mesmo que X'): 考えてもみる. O equivalente coloquial é 〜たって: 届かないって言われたって ('mesmo que me digam que não chega'). Comum na fala coloquial e em letras.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: verb → te-form → + も (formal) / plain past → + たって (casual)

grammar_points.name: Casual contractions (わかんない, やっぱ, どっか, ポッケ)

explanation.en: The song is saturated with casual spoken contractions: わかんない (= わからない), やっぱ (= やっぱり), どっか (= どこか), ポッケ (= ポケット), メトル (= メートル). These give the speaker a young, conversational voice. Learners should recognize them in speech and anime but avoid them in formal writing.
explanation.es: La canción está llena de contracciones habladas: わかんない (= わからない), やっぱ (= やっぱり), どっか (= どこか), ポッケ (= ポケット). Dan un tono joven y coloquial. Reconocerlas en habla/anime, pero evitarlas en escritura formal.
explanation.pt-BR: A música é cheia de contrações da fala cotidiana: わかんない (= わからない), やっぱ (= やっぱり), どっか (= どこか), ポッケ (= ポケット). Dão voz jovem e coloquial. Reconhecer em fala/anime, mas evitar em escrita formal.

grammar_points.name: English lyrics in anime OST

explanation.en:
How it works: This song is entirely in English. Hiroyuki Sawano's Attack on Titan soundtrack frequently uses English vocal tracks to create emotional, cinematic moments. The choice of English adds a universal quality to the music.

Example from this song: 'Call Your Name' (GV version) is performed entirely in English by Gemie, one of Sawano's regular vocalists.

Note: While this doesn't teach Japanese grammar, recognizing the emotional vocabulary (loss, determination, hope) in English anime songs helps build context for similar themes expressed in Japanese lyrics across other AOT tracks.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: N/A — English lyrics, not Japanese conjugation

grammar_points.name: Past tense narration

explanation.en:
How it works: English past tense is formed by adding -ed to regular verbs or using irregular forms. In Japanese, the past tense (た-form / ta-form) is used similarly for narration.

Example from this song: 'lost', 'gave', 'dreamt' — irregular English past tenses narrating loss and sacrifice.

Japanese equivalents:
• 'lost' → 失った (ushinatta, from 失う/ushinau, 'to lose')
• 'gave' → 与えた (ataeta, from 与える/ataeru, 'to give')
• 'dreamt' → 夢見た (yumemita, from 夢見る/yumemiru, 'to dream')

Note: Both languages use past tense for emotional narration in songs. Japanese た-form can also express discovery or sudden realization, not just past events.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: lose → lost, give → gave, dream → dreamt / Japanese: 失う (ushinau) → 失った (ushinatta), 与える (ataeru) → 与えた (ataeta)

grammar_points.name: Present continuous for emotion

explanation.en:
How it works: English present continuous ('am/is/are + -ing') expresses ongoing emotional states. The Japanese equivalent is 〜ている (te-iru), which shows both ongoing actions and resulting states.

Example from this song: 'I'm crying', 'I'm standing' — present continuous expressing raw, ongoing emotion.

Japanese equivalents:
• 'I'm crying' → 泣いている (naiteiru, from 泣く/naku, 'to cry')
• 'I'm standing' → 立っている (tatteiru, from 立つ/tatsu, 'to stand')
• 'I'm waiting' → 待っている (matteiru, from 待つ/matsu, 'to wait')

Note: In casual Japanese, ている contracts to てる: 泣いてる (naiteru), 立ってる (tatteru). This contraction is very common in anime dialogue and song lyrics.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: cry → I'm crying / Japanese: 泣く (naku, 'to cry') → 泣いている (naiteiru, 'am crying') → 泣いてる (naiteru, casual)

grammar_points.name: 〜ても / 〜てもかまわない (te mo / te mo kamawanai: even if / don't mind even if)

explanation.en:
〜ても after a verb te-form = 'even if (X)'. Add かまわない / いい for 'it doesn't matter even if / it's fine even if'.

From this song: 嘲ってもかまわない = 'I don't mind even if (someone) mocks'.

More examples:
• 失敗してもかまわない (it's okay to fail)
• 行ってもいい？(Can I go?)
• 雨が降っても行く (I'll go even if it rains)

grammar_points.name: 〜せる / 〜させる (causative: make someone do)

explanation.en:
Causative suffix attaches to the negative stem of a verb. Godan → 〜せる; ichidan → 〜させる. Means 'make/let X do'.

From this song: キラめかせる = '(something) makes X sparkle' — causative of キラめく.

More examples:
• 子供を寝させる (put the child to bed)
• 彼を待たせる (make him wait)
• 花を咲かせる (make flowers bloom)

grammar_points.conjugation_path: キラめく → キラめか (neg. stem) + せる → キラめかせる

grammar_points.name: 〜過ぎる (sugiru: too much)

explanation.en:
Attaches to the stem of a verb or adjective to mean 'too (X)'. い-adjective: drop い + 過ぎる; な-adjective: drop な + 過ぎる.

From this song: 眩し過ぎ = 'too dazzling' (truncated 眩し過ぎる).

More examples:
• 食べ過ぎる (eat too much)
• 高すぎる (too expensive)
• 静かすぎる (too quiet)

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 眩しい → 眩し + 過ぎる → 眩し過ぎる

grammar_points.name: 〜ような / 〜ように (you na / you ni: like / as if)

explanation.en:
Draws a comparison — 'like / resembling / in the manner of'. ような modifies a noun; ように modifies a verb or clause.

From this song: 夜明けを呼び覚ますような燃えるキモチ = 'a burning feeling like one that calls the dawn'.

More examples:
• 夢のような日 (a dream-like day)
• 泣いているように見える (looks as if crying)
• 鳥が飛ぶように (like a bird flies)

grammar_points.name: 〜ていく / 〜てくる (te iku / te kuru: progressive aspect)

explanation.en:
〜ていく after a verb's te-form = 'go on Xing / progress away from now'. 〜てくる = 'come toward / start happening'.

From this song:
• 追いかけてく (contracted 追いかけていく) = 'keep chasing (into the future)'
• つかまえてく = 'keep catching'

More examples:
• 変わっていく (gradually change)
• 雨が降ってくる (rain starts coming down)
• 年を取っていく (age gradually)

grammar_points.name: 〜ちゃう / 〜てしまう (chau / te shimau: do completely / end up doing)

explanation.en:
Attach to the te-form of a verb to express completion or an unintended result. 〜てしまう is the formal version; 〜ちゃう is its colloquial contraction.

From this song: かわしちゃう = 'brush (it) off (completely / casually)'.

More examples:
• 食べちゃう (eat up)
• 忘れちゃった (ended up forgetting)
• 行っちゃえ (just go already)

grammar_points.name: 〜てあげる (te ageru: do X for someone)

explanation.en:
Attach to the te-form of a verb to express doing the action for someone else's benefit. The speaker is the giver of the action.

From this song: 抱いてあげるよ = 'I'll hold you (for your sake)'.

More examples:
• 教えてあげる (I'll teach you)
• 手伝ってあげる (I'll help)
• 買ってあげる (I'll buy it for you)

Note: can sound condescending if used to superiors — use 〜てくれる / 〜てさしあげる depending on direction.

grammar_points.name: Imperative (〜え / 〜ろ: blunt command)

explanation.en:
The blunt imperative form: godan verbs end in 〜e (走る → 走れ); ichidan verbs end in 〜ろ (食べる → 食べろ). Used in songs for punch; in real life it's quite rough.

From this song: 走れ = 'Run!'.

More examples:
• 急げ (hurry up)
• 信じろ (believe)
• 食べろ (eat!)

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 走る → 走れ

translations.en: My first visit to the Louvre,
translations.es: Mi primera visita al Louvre

literal_meaning.en: First-time's Louvre (topic)

translations.en: ...wasn't anything to write home about
translations.es: ...no fue para tanto
translations.pt-BR: ...não foi nada de outro mundo

literal_meaning.en: Anything-special (topic) wasn't (feminine)

cultural_context.en: なんてことない is the idiom for 'no big deal / nothing special'. Sentence-final わ is a gently feminine softener — common in older women's speech, female narrators in songs and novels.

meaning.en: had already met (= 出会っていた)

translations.en: Because I'd long since met my own private Mona Lisa
translations.es: Porque hacía tiempo que yo ya había encontrado mi propia Mona Lisa
translations.pt-BR: Porque há muito tempo eu já tinha encontrado a minha própria Mona Lisa

literal_meaning.en: I only's Mona Lisa, already long-ago had-met because

cultural_context.en: とっくに ('long ago / already by') is a casual/literary intensifier of 'already'. The line frames the listener as a more precious, secret artwork than the world's most famous painting.

translations.en: The day I first saw you — gears that started turning
translations.es: El día en que te vi por primera vez — engranajes que se pusieron a girar
translations.pt-BR: O dia em que vi você pela primeira vez — engrenagens que começaram a girar

literal_meaning.en: First-time you (object) saw, that day, started-moving gears

cultural_context.en: 歯車 ('gear / cog') is a key Evangelion image — the franchise loves machinery imagery for fate and inevitability. 動き出した歯車 = 'gears that have begun turning' is a stock fatalism phrase.

translations.en: An unstoppable foreboding of loss
translations.es: Un presentimiento de pérdida que no se puede frenar
translations.pt-BR: Um pressentimento de perda que não dá pra parar

literal_meaning.en: Can't-be-stopped, loss's premonition

cultural_context.en: 喪失 ('loss / bereavement') is a heavy, formal noun — closer to 'bereavement' than the everyday 失う ('lose'). Pairs with 予感 ('premonition') for the sensation of a dread you can't justify yet.

translations.en: I already have plenty — but let's add one more
translations.es: Ya tengo un montón — pero añadamos uno más
translations.pt-BR: Já tem um monte — mas vamos somar mais uma

literal_meaning.en: Already lots exists but, one-more let's-increase

cultural_context.en: 増やす ('to increase') is the transitive partner of 増える ('to increase, intransitive'). Volitional polite 〜ましょう = 'let's do X'. The line is a soft invitation: one more memory to add to the pile.

grammar_points.name: Verb stem + たい / たくない / たくても (want to / don't want to / even if I want)

explanation.en: Verb stem + たい (want), たくない (don't want), たくても (even if I want). Conjugates like an い-adjective: 忘れたい → 忘れたくない → 忘れたくても → 忘れたくなかった. Only for the speaker's own desires.
explanation.es: Raíz verbal + たい (querer), たくない (no querer), たくても (aunque quiera). Se conjuga como adjetivo い: 忘れたい → 忘れたくない → 忘れたくても → 忘れたくなかった. Solo para los deseos propios.
explanation.pt-BR: Raiz verbal + たい (querer), たくない (não querer), たくても (mesmo querendo). Conjuga como adjetivo い: 忘れたい → 忘れたくない → 忘れたくても → 忘れたくなかった. Só para desejos do próprio falante.

grammar_points.name: Verb stem + ふり(を)する (pretend to)

explanation.en: ふり means 'a pretense / an act'. Verb-dictionary or adjective + ふりをする ('pretend to'): 知らないふり ('pretend not to know'), 寝たふり ('pretend to be asleep'), 寂しくないふり ('pretend not to be lonely'). The を often drops in casual speech.
explanation.es: ふり significa 'fingimiento'. Verbo en diccionario o adjetivo + ふりをする ('fingir que'): 知らないふり, 寝たふり, 寂しくないふり. El を suele caerse en habla casual.
explanation.pt-BR: ふり significa 'fingimento'. Verbo no dicionário ou adjetivo + ふりをする ('fingir que'): 知らないふり, 寝たふり, 寂しくないふり. O を costuma cair na fala casual.

grammar_points.name: Potential negative 〜られない (can't / unable to)

explanation.en: Adding 〜られる to a verb stem creates the potential ('can do X'). Negate with 〜られない ('can't do X'): 忘れられない ('can't forget'), 止められない ('can't stop'). Common to drop the ら in casual speech ('ら抜き'): 忘れれない. The full form is shown in standard writing.
explanation.es: Añadir 〜られる a la raíz verbal forma el potencial ('poder hacer X'). Negativo: 〜られない ('no poder'): 忘れられない, 止められない. En el habla casual se puede omitir ら ('ら抜き'): 忘れれない.
explanation.pt-BR: Adicionar 〜られる à raiz verbal cria o potencial ('conseguir fazer X'). Negativo: 〜られない ('não conseguir'): 忘れられない, 止められない. Pode-se omitir ら na fala casual ('ら抜き'): 忘れれない.

grammar_points.name: Verb-dictionary + ような (like / a kind of)

explanation.en: Verb-dictionary + ような turns a verb into a descriptor: 燃えるようなキス ('a kiss like burning / an inflammatory kiss'); 泣きそうな顔 ('a face like about to cry'); 飛ぶような速さ ('flying-fast'). Adverbial form is ように.
explanation.es: Verbo en diccionario + ような convierte un verbo en descriptor: 燃えるようなキス, 泣きそうな顔, 飛ぶような速さ. La forma adverbial es ように.
explanation.pt-BR: Verbo no dicionário + ような transforma um verbo em descritor: 燃えるようなキス, 泣きそうな顔, 飛ぶような速さ. A forma adverbial é ように.

grammar_points.name: Layered conditional: 〜たくても 〜られないほど

explanation.en: Stacked: 〜たい (want) + 〜ても (even if) + potential negative + ほど (to the extent). 忘れたくても 忘れられないほど = 'so [intense] that even if I want to forget, I can't'. Three N3 grammar points working together to express devastating intensity.
explanation.es: Apilamiento: 〜たい (querer) + 〜ても (aunque) + potencial negativo + ほど (hasta el punto de). 忘れたくても 忘れられないほど = 'tan intenso que, aunque quiera olvidar, no puedo'. Tres puntos N3 juntos.
explanation.pt-BR: Empilhamento: 〜たい (querer) + 〜ても (mesmo que) + potencial negativo + ほど (a tal ponto). 忘れたくても 忘れられないほど = 'tão intenso que, mesmo querendo esquecer, eu não consigo'. Três pontos N3 juntos.

explanation.en: 取る ('to take') forms many fixed idioms with body/age nouns: 年を取る ('to age', literally 'take on years'), 連絡を取る ('to make contact'), 手を取る ('to take hold of someone's hand'), 距離を取る ('to keep distance'). The verb 取る itself is concrete; the meaning is set by the noun.
explanation.es: 取る ('tomar') forma muchas expresiones fijas con sustantivos: 年を取る ('envejecer'), 連絡を取る ('ponerse en contacto'), 手を取る ('tomar la mano'), 距離を取る ('mantener distancia'). El verbo es concreto; el sustantivo fija el sentido.
explanation.pt-BR: 取る ('pegar') forma muitas expressões fixas com substantivos: 年を取る ('envelhecer'), 連絡を取る ('entrar em contato'), 手を取る ('pegar a mão'), 距離を取る ('manter distância'). O verbo é concreto; o substantivo define o sentido.

grammar_points.name: 〜なき (literary negation, 'without')

explanation.en:
How it works: なき (naki) is the classical/literary form of ない (nai, 'without/not'), used to modify nouns. It gives a poetic, timeless quality.

Example from this song: 終わりなき (owari naki) = 'endless / without end' — from 終わり (owari, 'end') + なき (naki, literary 'without')

More examples:
• 果てなき旅 (hate naki tabi, 'an endless journey') — from 果て (hate, 'end')
• 名もなき花 (na mo naki hana, 'a nameless flower') — from 名 (na, 'name')
• 限りなき愛 (kagiri naki ai, 'limitless love') — from 限り (kagiri, 'limit')

Note: なき is the literary equivalent of ない used as an adjective. Modern Japanese would say 終わりのない (owari no nai). なき appears in song titles, poetry, and formal writing for its elegance.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 終わり (owari, 'end') + なき (naki, literary 'without') → 終わりなき (owari naki, 'endless / without end')

grammar_points.name: 〜かけて (on the verge of)

explanation.en:
How it works: かける (kakeru) attached to a verb's masu-stem means 'about to,' 'on the verge of,' or 'half-done.' It expresses an incomplete or starting action.

Example from this song: 掴みかけて (tsukami kakete) = 'on the verge of grasping' — from 掴む (tsukamu, 'to grasp') → 掴み (tsukami, stem) + かけて (kakete)

More examples:
• 死にかける (shini kakeru, 'nearly die') — from 死ぬ (shinu, 'to die')
• 言いかけて止めた (ii kakete yameta, 'started to say but stopped') — from 言う (iu, 'to say')
• 食べかけのパン (tabe kake no pan, 'half-eaten bread') — from 食べる (taberu, 'to eat')

Note: 〜かけ as a noun modifier means 'half-done': 読みかけの本 (yomikake no hon, 'half-read book'). The て-form かけて connects to the next action: 'was on the verge of X, and then...'

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 掴む (tsukamu, 'to grasp') → 掴み (tsukami, stem) + かけて (kakete, 'on the verge of') → 掴みかけて (tsukami kakete, 'on the verge of grasping')

grammar_points.name: けして〜ない (never)

explanation.en:
How it works: けして (keshite) or 決して (keshite) combined with a negative verb means 'never' or 'by no means.' It creates an emphatic absolute negation.

Example from this song: The song uses けして...ない to express something that will absolutely never happen — an unbreakable resolve.

More examples:
• 決して忘れない (keshite wasurenai, 'I will never forget') — from 忘れる (wasureru, 'to forget')
• 決して諦めない (keshite akiramenai, 'I will never give up') — from 諦める (akirameru, 'to give up')
• 決して許さない (keshite yurusanai, 'I will never forgive') — from 許す (yurusu, 'to forgive')

Note: 決して must always pair with a negative form. Never use it with positive verbs. It's stronger than ぜんぜん〜ない (zenzen ~nai, 'not at all'). 決して expresses firm determination.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 決して (keshite, 'never') + verb negative form → 決して〜ない (keshite ~nai, 'absolutely never')

grammar_points.name: 〜ずに (without doing)

explanation.en:
How it works: ずに (zu ni) is the classical negative te-form meaning 'without doing.' Replace ない with ず and add に to connect to the next action.

Example from this song: 逸らさずに (sorasazu ni) = 'without averting (one's gaze)' — from 逸らす (sorasu, 'to avert') → 逸らさない (sorasanai) → 逸らさず (sorasazu) + に (ni)

More examples:
• 食べずに寝た (tabezu ni neta, 'slept without eating') — from 食べる (taberu, 'to eat')
• 迷わずに進む (mayowazu ni susumu, 'advance without hesitating') — from 迷う (mayou, 'to hesitate')
• 諦めずに頑張る (akiramezu ni ganbaru, 'keep trying without giving up')

Note: ずに = literary ないで. Exception: する → せずに (sezu ni), not しずに. ず can also stand alone without に in literary contexts: 言わず語らず (iwazu katarazu, 'without saying or telling').

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 逸らす (sorasu, 'to avert') → 逸らさない (sorasanai) → 逸らさず (sorasazu) + に (ni) → 逸らさずに (sorasazu ni, 'without averting')

grammar_points.name: 〜ために (for the sake of)

explanation.en:
How it works: ために (tame ni) expresses purpose ('in order to') or benefit ('for the sake of'). After a verb dictionary form, it means 'in order to do.' After a noun + の, it means 'for the sake of.'

Example from this song: The song uses ために to express what the speaker is striving for — the purpose behind their actions.

More examples:
• 合格するために勉強する (goukaku suru tame ni benkyou suru, 'study in order to pass')
• 家族のために働く (kazoku no tame ni hataraku, 'work for the family')
• 健康のために走る (kenkou no tame ni hashiru, 'run for health')

Note: Verb + ために = 'in order to (do).' Noun + のために = 'for the sake of (noun).' Compare with ように, which is for non-volitional results.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: verb dictionary form + ために (tame ni, 'in order to') / noun + の + ために (no tame ni, 'for the sake of')

grammar_points.name: 〜ていく (continuing into the future)

explanation.en:
How it works: ていく (te iku) expresses an action or change continuing from now into the future. It shows forward progression through time.

Example from this song: 生きていく (ikite iku) = 'will go on living' — from 生きる (ikiru, 'to live') → 生きて (ikite) + いく (iku, 'to go')

More examples:
• 強くなっていく (tsuyoku natte iku, 'getting stronger and stronger')
• 変わっていく (kawatte iku, 'keeps changing over time') — from 変わる (kawaru, 'to change')
• 学んでいく (manande iku, 'will continue learning') — from 学ぶ (manabu, 'to learn')

Note: ていく shows future-directed change. てくる shows past-to-present change. 生きていく is a powerful expression meaning 'I will go on living' — often used to express determination in the face of difficulty.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 生きる (ikiru, 'to live') → 生きて (ikite) + いく (iku, 'to go') → 生きていく (ikite iku, 'will go on living')

Example from this song: 揺らめきながら (yurameki nagara) = 'while flickering' — from 揺らめく (yurameku, 'to flicker') → 揺らめき (yurameki, stem) + ながら (nagara)

More examples:
• 音楽を聴きながら勉強する (ongaku o kiki nagara benkyou suru, 'study while listening to music')
• 歩きながら話す (aruki nagara hanasu, 'talk while walking')
• 泣きながら笑う (naki nagara warau, 'laugh while crying')

Note: The main action is the second verb (after ながら). The ながら verb is the background/simultaneous action. Both actions are done by the same person.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 揺らめく (yurameku, 'to flicker') → 揺らめき (yurameki, stem) + ながら (nagara, 'while') → 揺らめきながら (yurameki nagara, 'while flickering')

grammar_points.name: 〜ていく (continuing/progressing)

explanation.en:
How it works: ていく (te iku) expresses an action or change that continues from now into the future, or progresses away from the current point.

Example from this song: 変えていった (kaete itta) = 'kept changing (over time)' — from 変える (kaeru, 'to change') → 変えて (kaete) + いった (itta, past of iku)

More examples:
• 成長していく (seichou shite iku, 'keeps growing') — from 成長する (seichou suru, 'to grow')
• 忘れていく (wasurete iku, 'gradually forgetting') — from 忘れる (wasureru, 'to forget')
• 強くなっていく (tsuyoku natte iku, 'getting stronger and stronger')

Note: ていく = future/away direction. てくる = past-to-present/toward direction. Past tense ていった means this progression happened over time in the past.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 変える (kaeru, 'to change') → 変えて (kaete) → 変えていった (kaete itta, 'kept changing over time')

grammar_points.name: 〜としても (even if)

explanation.en:
How it works: としても (to shite mo) means 'even if' or 'even assuming that.' It presents a hypothetical condition and says the result holds regardless.

Example from this song: The song uses としても to express that even in a hypothetical worst case, something still holds true.

More examples:
• 雨だとしても行く (ame da to shite mo iku, 'I'll go even if it rains')
• 失敗したとしても後悔しない (shippai shita to shite mo koukai shinai, 'even if I fail, I won't regret it')
• 嘘だとしても嬉しい (uso da to shite mo ureshii, 'even if it's a lie, I'm happy')

Note: としても is more formal/hypothetical than ても. ても is 'even if (it happens),' while としても is 'even assuming/supposing that.'

grammar_points.conjugation_path: verb/noun + としても (to shite mo, 'even assuming that')

grammar_points.name: 〜かな (I wonder)

explanation.en:
How it works: かな (kana) is a sentence-ending particle expressing wondering or uncertainty. It's like thinking out loud: 'I wonder if...'

Example from this song: The song uses かな to express the singer's inner wondering and uncertainty about a situation.

More examples:
• 大丈夫かな (daijoubu kana, 'I wonder if it's OK')
• 明日は晴れるかな (ashita wa hareru kana, 'I wonder if it'll be sunny tomorrow')
• 好きなのかな (suki na no kana, 'I wonder if I like them')

Note: かな is softer and more introspective than か (ka, question marker). It's used for self-directed wondering, not direct questions to others. Very common in songs for expressing inner thoughts.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: plain form + かな (kana, 'I wonder')

grammar_points.name: 〜次第 (depends on; up to)

explanation.en:
How it works: 次第 (shidai) after a noun means 'depends on' or 'up to.' It indicates that the outcome is determined by the stated factor.

Example from this song: 自分次第 (jibun shidai) = 'up to myself / depends on me' — from 自分 (jibun, 'oneself') + 次第 (shidai)

More examples:
• 天気次第 (tenki shidai, 'depends on the weather') — from 天気 (tenki, 'weather')
• やり方次第 (yarikata shidai, 'depends on how you do it') — from やり方 (yarikata, 'method')
• 気持ち次第 (kimochi shidai, 'depends on your feelings') — from 気持ち (kimochi, 'feelings')

Note: Noun + 次第 is a very empowering expression. 自分次第 means 'it's all up to me' — a common motivational phrase. 次第 can also mean 'as soon as' with verb stems: 届き次第 (todoki shidai, 'as soon as it arrives').

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 自分 (jibun, 'oneself') + 次第 (shidai, 'depends on') → 自分次第 (jibun shidai, 'up to myself')

grammar_points.name: 〜たら (if/when conditional)

explanation.en:
How it works: たら (tara) is a conditional meaning 'if' or 'when.' Form it by adding ら to the past tense (ta-form) of a verb or adjective.

Example from this song: 埋められたら (umeraretara) = 'if I could fill (the gap)' — from 埋める (umeru, 'to fill') → potential: 埋められる (umerareru) → past: 埋められた (umerareta) + ら (ra)

More examples:
• 食べたら (tabetara, 'if/when you eat') — from 食べる (taberu, 'to eat')
• 安かったら買う (yasukattara kau, 'if it's cheap, I'll buy it') — from 安い (yasui, 'cheap')
• 暇だったら来て (hima dattara kite, 'if you're free, come over') — from 暇 (hima, 'free')

Note: たら is the most versatile conditional — it works for hypothetical ('if'), temporal ('when'), and counterfactual ('if only'). It's often the safest conditional to use when unsure.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 埋める (umeru, 'to fill') → 埋められる (umerareru, potential) → 埋められた (umerareta, past) + ら (ra) → 埋められたら (umeraretara, 'if I could fill')
