translations.en: Broken, pale wings — you just got tired from a sky that was a little too blue.
translations.es: Alas frágiles y rotas — solo te cansaste de un cielo demasiado azul.
translations.pt-BR: Asas frágeis e quebradas — você só ficou cansado de um céu azul demais.

literal_meaning.en: 'Broken faint wings — you [topic] a-little too-blue sky by got-tired just.' 〜すぎる attaches to adjectives to mean 'too (much)'. さ at sentence end softens the assertion.

cultural_context.en: 青すぎる空 ('too-blue sky') is a bittersweet image common in Japanese lyrics — a sky so beautiful it becomes oppressive, exhausting to live under.

translations.en: It's okay to smile for yourself now, not for someone else.
translations.es: Está bien sonreír para ti mismo ahora, no por alguien más.
translations.pt-BR: Tá tudo bem sorrir por você mesmo agora, não pelos outros.

literal_meaning.en: 'no-longer someone-of sake not-but, self-of sake for smile good.' 〜て+いい = 'it's okay to (do X)'. じゃなくて is the connecting negative form.

translations.en: Loneliness still creeps in — a candle burning somewhere inside me.
translations.es: La soledad sigue acechando — una vela encendida en mi interior.
translations.pt-BR: A solidão continua a se aproximar — uma vela acesa lá dentro.

literal_meaning.en: 'As-before creeping-close solitude — inside [loc] lit candle.' Two noun fragments juxtaposed: an external encroachment and an internal tiny flame.

cultural_context.en: The pairing of 忍びよる (sneaking up on prey) with 孤独 gives loneliness a predatory character, while 蝋燭 evokes tiny vulnerable resistance — a moth-and-flame dynamic turned inward.

translations.en: Contrary to the lively party and its luxurious chandeliers —
translations.es: En contraste con la fiesta animada y sus lujosos candelabros —
translations.pt-BR: Ao contrário da festa animada e dos seus lustres luxuosos —

literal_meaning.en: 'bustling party — luxurious chandelier with contrary.' 裏腹に = 'the opposite / at odds with' — typically signals that the speaker's inner state contradicts what's outwardly visible.

translations.en: With what should I fill the hollow of unsaid words?
translations.es: ¿Con qué debería llenar el hueco de las palabras que faltan?
translations.pt-BR: Com o quê eu deveria preencher o vazio das palavras que faltaram?

literal_meaning.en: 'insufficient words-of hollow [obj] with-what fill-if good the-one I-wonder.' 〜たらいい = 'it would be good to/if' — asks what action would resolve a dilemma.

translations.en: I don't know anymore.
translations.es: Ya no sé.
translations.pt-BR: Já não sei mais.

literal_meaning.en: 'no-longer don't-know [resignation].' The end particle や softens the statement into a sigh.

translations.en: At least inside a dream —
translations.es: Al menos dentro de un sueño —
translations.pt-BR: Pelo menos dentro de um sonho —

literal_meaning.en: 'at-least dream-of inside at —' A conditional preamble, setting up the next line's hypothetical.

translations.en: — even a sky like that wouldn't be needed, if only I could swim freely.
translations.es: — ni siquiera necesitaría un cielo así, si pudiera nadar libremente.
translations.pt-BR: — eu nem precisaria daquele céu, se conseguisse nadar livremente.

literal_meaning.en: 'freely could-swim-if, that-kind-of sky even don't-need even-though.' のに closes a hypothesis with bittersweet 'but that's not how it is' regret.

translations.en: Everything up until yesterday —
translations.es: Todo lo de hasta ayer —
translations.pt-BR: Tudo que aconteceu até ontem —

literal_meaning.en: 'yesterday-until-of things [obj].' A hanging object clause that the next line resolves.

translations.en: — even without painting it over, you can still face tomorrow.
translations.es: — incluso sin borrarlo, puedes enfrentar el mañana.
translations.pt-BR: — mesmo sem apagá-lo, você consegue encarar o amanhã.

literal_meaning.en: 'without-painting-over-even tomorrow toward can-face even-though.' 塗り潰す literally 'paint-crush' — to fill in completely.

cultural_context.en: 塗り潰す is a painter's verb: to cover a canvas completely so nothing of what was there shows. The line is saying you don't have to erase yesterday to go on.

translations.en: Making peace with my inferiority complex — that's not easy to pull off.
translations.es: Reconciliarme con mi complejo de inferioridad — eso no se da tan fácil.
translations.pt-BR: Fazer as pazes com o meu complexo de inferioridade — não sai fácil.

literal_meaning.en: 'inferiority-complex with-of reconciliation [topic] easily-[contrastive] won't-be-granted.' は after the adverb 簡単に emphasises 'easily, at least, it won't happen'.

translations.en: A mirror perched on the summit of self-consciousness — and the flower petals it reflects.
translations.es: Un espejo posado en la cima de la autoconciencia — y los pétalos que refleja.
translations.pt-BR: Um espelho pousado no topo da autoconsciência — e as pétalas de flor que ele reflete.

literal_meaning.en: 'self-consciousness-of summit at sit mirror [subj] reflects flower-petals.' The mirror-as-sitter metaphor portrays self-awareness as a detached observer watching delicate beauty.

cultural_context.en: The mirror and flower-petal pairing evokes Buddhist metaphors for the illusory self — seeing what passes (petals) in a reflective surface that isn't truly the thing itself.

meaning.en: as if; in the manner of

translations.en: I try to scream a love that's gone stiff, as if wringing it out of me — but —
translations.es: Intento gritar un amor ya endurecido, como arrancándolo de mí — pero —
translations.pt-BR: Tento gritar um amor endurecido, como se o arrancasse de mim — mas —

literal_meaning.en: 'wring-out like-that hardened love [obj] shout try but.' 〜てみる = 'try doing'. 凝れた is literary for 'stiffened / clotted'.

translations.en: it's just frustrating.
translations.es: solo me frustra.
translations.pt-BR: é só frustrante.

literal_meaning.en: Single-adjective line in 〜て form — leaves the thought open, as if trailing off.

translations.en: Inside time's cycles —
translations.es: Dentro del ciclo del tiempo —
translations.pt-BR: Dentro do tempo que gira —

literal_meaning.en: 'cycling time-of inside at —' 巡る carries the sense of coming back around.

translations.en: The wound will eventually turn into a scab.
translations.es: La herida, con el tiempo, se vuelve costra.
translations.pt-BR: A ferida, aos poucos, vira casca.

literal_meaning.en: 'wound [topic] before-long scab into changing-goes.' 〜ていく = 'gradually becoming', moving away from the present state over time.

translations.en: But you didn't wait for that.
translations.es: Pero tú no esperaste eso.
translations.pt-BR: Mas você não esperou por isso.

literal_meaning.en: 'you [topic] that [obj] not-waiting.' 〜ず is the classical literary negative ending; feels more elegiac than 〜ないで.

translations.en: Beautifully —
translations.es: Con gran belleza —
translations.pt-BR: Com uma beleza imensa —

literal_meaning.en: 'very beautifully —' Adverbial fragment, flowing into the next line.

translations.en: — and so fleeting.
translations.es: — y tan efímera.
translations.pt-BR: — e tão efêmera.

literal_meaning.en: 'very fleeting-looking and.' はかなげ = hakanai (fleeting) + げ (appearance of); so 'looking fleeting/ephemeral'.

cultural_context.en: はかなげ invokes the Japanese aesthetic of mono no aware — the poignant awareness of impermanence — and typically describes something beautiful precisely because it won't last.

meaning.en: sunny spot; warm patch of sunlight

translations.en: A prayer trembling in a sunbeam, like baby-down left after the hair falls away.
translations.es: Una plegaria que tiembla en un rayo de sol, como la pelusa que queda cuando el pelo cae.
translations.pt-BR: Uma oração tremendo na réstia de sol, como a penugem que fica depois que o pelo cai.

literal_meaning.en: 'peeled-fallen after-of baby-down like sunlit-spot-of within at trembling prayer.' Dense noun-modifying chain — the prayer is compared to the fine remainder-hair.

cultural_context.en: 産毛 (ubuge) is the fine baby-fuzz on a newborn — pairing it with 'after the (outer) feathers peeled away' makes the prayer simultaneously newborn-fragile and remnant.

translations.en: It's okay not to force yourself to love someone right now.
translations.es: Está bien no forzarte a amar a alguien ahora mismo.
translations.pt-BR: Tá tudo bem não se forçar a amar alguém agora.

literal_meaning.en: 'now [topic] forcibly someone-of thing [obj] let's-love quotatively not-think even-though.' 〜と思う = 'think that...'; volitional+と思う = 'think of doing'.

translations.en: Sometimes this world, looking upward —
translations.es: A veces este mundo, al mirar hacia arriba —
translations.pt-BR: Às vezes, este mundo, ao olhar pra cima —

literal_meaning.en: 'sometimes this world [topic] up [obj] facing —' 上を向く is the classic 'look upward' idiom, here hanging into the next line.

translations.en: — is a little too dazzling to walk through, isn't it.
translations.es: — es un poco demasiado deslumbrante para caminar así, ¿no?
translations.pt-BR: — é ofuscante demais pra atravessar caminhando, né.

literal_meaning.en: 'walk in-order-to a-little too-dazzling [confirm].' 〜には after a dictionary-form verb = 'in order to (do)'.

translations.en: When I lower my eyes, as if sinking —
translations.es: Cuando bajo la mirada, como si me hundiera —
translations.pt-BR: Quando baixo os olhos, como se afundasse —

literal_meaning.en: 'sink like-that eyes [obj] lower when.' ~と (conditional/temporal) = 'when / whenever (X happens)'.

translations.en: — the parched ground slurps up my tears.
translations.es: — la tierra seca se bebe mis lágrimas.
translations.pt-BR: — o chão ressequido bebe as minhas lágrimas.

literal_meaning.en: 'dried ground [subj] tears [obj] slurps.' The verb すする (usually for noodles/soup) is violent here — the ground is drinking the tears like broth.

cultural_context.en: すする is onomatopoeic for slurping — ramen, udon. Applying it to dry earth drinking tears is jarringly visceral, a trademark of Aqua Timez's lyrical style.

translations.en: You don't have to catch and hold everything.
translations.es: No tienes que absorberlo todo.
translations.pt-BR: Você não precisa absorver tudo.

literal_meaning.en: 'everything [obj] not-accepting-even good [emph].' 〜なくてもいい = 'don't have to (do)'. 受けとめる = 'catch and hold', not just 'accept'.

translations.en: Enduring isn't the only form of courage.
translations.es: Aguantarse no es la única clase de valentía.
translations.pt-BR: Aguentar não é a única forma de coragem.

literal_meaning.en: 'endure act-of only [subj] courage is-not.' The contrastive が plus だけ emphasises the isolation — 'only enduring, that alone, isn't courage'.

cultural_context.en: A gentle rebuke of Japanese social stoicism — the cultural ideal of 我慢 (gaman, endurance) is here softly challenged: courage can also mean letting go.

grammar_points.name: 〜すぎる (sugiru: too / excessively)

explanation.en:
Attaches to the stem of a verb, or to an い-adjective (dropping 〜い), or to a な-adjective (dropping な), to mean 'too / excessively'.

Examples from this song:
• 青すぎる (aosugiru) = too blue — 青い → 青 + すぎる
• 眩しすぎる (mabushisugiru) = too dazzling — 眩しい → 眩し + すぎる

More examples:
• 食べすぎる (overeat)
• 高すぎる (too expensive)
• 静かすぎる (too quiet — 静か(な) → 静か + すぎる)

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 青い → 青 (stem) + すぎる → 青すぎる

grammar_points.name: 〜なくてもいい (nakute mo ii: don't have to)

explanation.en:
Negative 〜て form + も + いい — 'it's okay even if not (doing)' — gives permission to not do something.

Examples from this song:
• 塗り潰さなくても 明日に向かえる (even without painting it over, you can face tomorrow)
• 全てを受けとめなくてもいい (you don't have to take in everything)
• 愛そうと思わなくていい (you don't have to think of loving)

More examples:
• 行かなくてもいい (you don't have to go)
• 急がなくてもいい (no need to hurry)
• 謝らなくてもいい (you don't need to apologize)

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 受けとめる → 受けとめない (neg) → 受けとめなくて (neg te-form) + も + いい

explanation.en:
Placed at the end of a clause to express 'even though / despite (X)'. Carries a bittersweet / regretful tone — often 'if only X, then Y'.

Examples from this song:
• いらないのに (even though [it] isn't needed)
• 明日に向かえるのに (even though you can face tomorrow)
• 思わなくていいのに (even though you don't have to)

More examples:
• 寒いのに薄着だ (Even though it's cold, (they're) lightly dressed)
• もう遅いのに (Even though it's already late)
• 知っているのに教えてくれない (Even though (they) know, (they) won't tell me)

Note: けど/が are neutral contrasts; のに carries emotional weight — disappointment, frustration, longing.

grammar_points.name: 〜ように (you ni: as if / in the manner of / so that)

explanation.en:
After a verb (dictionary or negative form), means 'as if / so as to / in the manner of'. Shape-shifts based on what the speaker wants to express.

Examples from this song:
• 振り絞るように (as if wringing it out)
• 沈むように目を伏せる (lower eyes as if sinking)
• 産毛のように震える (tremble like baby-down)

More examples:
• 風邪を引かないように気をつける (be careful so as not to catch a cold)
• 鳥が飛ぶように (like a bird flies)
• 分かりやすいように説明する (explain so it's easy to understand)

grammar_points.name: 〜ず (zu: classical literary negative)

explanation.en:
Literary/archaic negative suffix attached to a verb's negative stem. Equivalent to 〜ないで / 〜ずに in meaning. Gives a poetic, formal, or solemn tone.

Examples from this song:
• 待たず (without waiting)
• 知らず知らずのうちに (before one knows it)

More examples:
• 何も言わず去った (left without saying anything)
• 思わず笑う (involuntarily laugh)
• 休まず働く (work without resting)

Note: する → せず (irregular). 来る → 来ず (こず).

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 待つ → 待た (neg. stem) + ず → 待たず

grammar_points.name: 〜げ (ge: gives the appearance of)

explanation.en:
A suffix attached to the stem of an い-adjective (drop 〜い) or to certain nouns/adjectives, meaning 'looks / seems / gives the appearance of (X)'.

Example from this song:
• はかなげ (hakanage) = はかない (fleeting) → はかな + げ = 'seemingly fleeting, wistful-looking'

More examples:
• 不安げ (fuange) = looking anxious
• 寂しげ (sabishige) = looking lonely
• 大人げ (otonage) = having an adult's demeanor
• 親しげ (shitashige) = seeming friendly

Note: 〜げ + な = attributive form (e.g. 不安げな顔 = anxious-looking face).

grammar_points.conjugation_path: はかない → はかな (stem) + げ → はかなげ

grammar_points.name: Compound verbs with 〜落ちる / 〜潰す / 〜絞る (verb + verb)

explanation.en:
Japanese freely joins verbs by attaching the second verb to the stem form of the first. The second verb modifies how the first happens.

Examples from this song:
• 剥がれ落ちる (hagareochiru) = 剥がれる (peel) + 落ちる (fall) = 'peel off and fall'
• 塗り潰す (nuritsubusu) = 塗る (paint) + 潰す (crush/flatten) = 'paint out completely'
• 振り絞る (furishiboru) = 振る (shake) + 絞る (wring) = 'wring out with effort'
• 忍び寄る (shinobiyoru) = 忍ぶ (sneak) + 寄る (approach) = 'creep up'

The second verb often answers 'how / how thoroughly' — crushed, wrung, sneakily, etc.

grammar_points.name: 〜のように見える (no you ni mieru: looks like)

explanation.en:
How it works: のように見える (no you ni mieru) means 'looks like' or 'appears to be.' It combines the comparison pattern のように (no you ni, 'like') with 見える (mieru, 'to be visible/appear').

Example from this song: 山のように見える (yama no you ni mieru) = 'looks like a mountain' — comparing something's appearance to a mountain

More examples:
• 子供のように見える (kodomo no you ni mieru, 'looks like a child') — from 子供 (kodomo, 'child')
• 簡単なように見える (kantan na you ni mieru, 'looks easy') — from 簡単 (kantan, 'simple')
• 怒っているように見える (okotte iru you ni mieru, 'looks angry') — from 怒る (okoru, 'to get angry')

Note: のように is for nouns, なように is for na-adjectives, and plain form + ように is for verbs. 見える means something appears that way to the observer — it's not necessarily the truth.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 山 (yama, 'mountain') + の (no) + ように (you ni, 'like') + 見える (mieru, 'appears') → 山のように見える (yama no you ni mieru, 'looks like a mountain')

grammar_points.name: 〜のために (no tame ni: for the sake of)

explanation.en:
How it works: のために (no tame ni) means 'for the sake of' or 'for the benefit of.' After a noun, it expresses who or what something is done for.

Example from this song: 世のために人のために (yo no tame ni hito no tame ni) = 'for the world, for the people' — from 世 (yo, 'world') and 人 (hito, 'people')

More examples:
• 家族のために働く (kazoku no tame ni hataraku, 'work for the sake of family') — from 家族 (kazoku, 'family')
• 健康のために運動する (kenkou no tame ni undou suru, 'exercise for health') — from 健康 (kenkou, 'health')
• 将来のために勉強する (shourai no tame ni benkyou suru, 'study for the future')

Note: Noun + のために = 'for the sake of (noun).' Verb dictionary form + ために = 'in order to (do).' The first is about beneficiary, the second is about purpose.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 世 (yo, 'world') + の (no) + ために (tame ni, 'for the sake of') → 世のために (yo no tame ni, 'for the world')

grammar_points.name: 〜に敗れる (ni yabureru: to be defeated by)

explanation.en:
How it works: に敗れる (ni yabureru) means 'to be defeated by' or 'to lose to.' The particle に marks what defeated you, and 敗れる (yabureru) means 'to be defeated.'

Example from this song: 夢に敗れる (yume ni yabureru) = 'to be defeated by a dream / to have a dream crushed' — from 夢 (yume, 'dream')

More examples:
• 試合に敗れる (shiai ni yabureru, 'to lose the match') — from 試合 (shiai, 'match')
• 相手に敗れた (aite ni yabureta, 'was defeated by the opponent') — from 相手 (aite, 'opponent')
• 現実に敗れる (genjitsu ni yabureru, 'defeated by reality') — from 現実 (genjitsu, 'reality')

Note: 敗れる (yabureru) is more literary/formal than 負ける (makeru, 'to lose'). In songs and poetry, 夢に敗れる conveys having your dreams crushed or failing to achieve them.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 夢 (yume, 'dream') + に (ni, 'by') + 敗れる (yabureru, 'to be defeated') → 夢に敗れる (yume ni yabureru, 'defeated by a dream')

grammar_points.name: 〜たまに (tama ni: occasionally)

explanation.en:
How it works: たまに (tama ni) is an adverb meaning 'occasionally,' 'once in a while,' or 'from time to time.' It describes actions that happen infrequently.

Example from this song: 僕たまに (boku tama ni) = 'I sometimes...' — the speaker admits they occasionally do something

More examples:
• たまに映画を見る (tama ni eiga o miru, 'occasionally watch movies') — from 映画 (eiga, 'movie')
• たまには休もう (tama ni wa yasumou, 'let's rest once in a while') — with は for emphasis
• たまに会う友達 (tama ni au tomodachi, 'a friend I meet occasionally') — from 会う (au, 'to meet')

Note: Frequency scale: いつも (itsumo, 'always') > よく (yoku, 'often') > 時々 (tokidoki, 'sometimes') > たまに (tama ni, 'occasionally') > めったに〜ない (metta ni ~nai, 'rarely'). たまには (tama ni wa) with は is used for suggestions: 'for once, let's...'

grammar_points.conjugation_path: たまに (tama ni, 'occasionally') — adverb, placed before the verb

grammar_points.name: 〜故に (yue ni - because of)

explanation.en:
A literary and formal way to say "because of" or "due to." It sounds much more elegant than the everyday から (kara) or ので (node). You will mostly find it in written Japanese, poetry, and song lyrics.

How it works:
Attach 故に (yue ni) after a verb in past tense, a noun, or a na-adjective + な. It marks the reason or cause for what follows.

Example from this song:
愛した故に芽生えた悪の花 (aishita yue ni mebaeta aku no hana, "Because I loved, a flower of evil bloomed")

More examples:
- 若さ故に (wakasa yue ni, "because of youth")
- 知らなかった故に (shiranakatta yue ni, "because I did not know")
- 彼女が好きだった故に (kanojo ga suki datta yue ni, "because I liked her")

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 愛する (aisuru) → 愛した (aishita) → 愛した故に (aishita yue ni)

grammar_points.name: 〜であろう (de arou - probably is/will be)

explanation.en:
A formal way to express conjecture or probability, similar to "will probably be" or "is likely." This is the volitional form of である (de aru), which is the formal equivalent of だ (da). You will encounter it in literature, formal speeches, and dramatic lyrics.

How it works:
Place であろう (de arou) after a noun or na-adjective stem. It replaces だろう (darou) in formal/literary registers.

Example from this song:
これから先訪れるであろう全てを (korekara saki otozureru de arou subete o, "Everything that will likely come from here on")

More examples:
- 困難であろう (konnan de arou, "it will probably be difficult")
- 彼は天才であろう (kare wa tensai de arou, "he is probably a genius")
- 正しいであろう判断 (tadashii de arou handan, "a judgment that is probably correct")

grammar_points.conjugation_path: である (de aru) → であろう (de arou, volitional conjecture)

grammar_points.name: 〜ワケにはいかない (wake ni wa ikanai - cannot do)

explanation.en:
Expresses that something "cannot be done" due to social, moral, or situational reasons. It is stronger than できない (dekinai, "cannot") because it implies the speaker feels a moral or social obligation not to do something.

How it works:
Attach ワケにはいかない (wake ni wa ikanai) after the dictionary form of a verb. The verb describes the action that is unacceptable.

Example from this song:
誰にも邪魔させるワケにはいかないから (dare ni mo jama saseru wake ni wa ikanai kara, "Because I cannot allow anyone to get in the way")

More examples:
- ここで諦めるワケにはいかない (koko de akirameru wake ni wa ikanai, "I cannot give up here")
- 嘘をつくワケにはいかない (uso o tsuku wake ni wa ikanai, "I cannot tell a lie")
- 友達を裏切るワケにはいかない (tomodachi o uragiru wake ni wa ikanai, "I cannot betray my friend")

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 邪魔する (jama suru) → 邪魔させる (jama saseru, causative) + ワケにはいかない (wake ni wa ikanai)

grammar_points.name: 〜させる (saseru - causative form)

explanation.en:
The causative form expresses "make someone do" or "let someone do" something. It is one of the key verb conjugations in Japanese.

How it works:
For ichidan (ru-) verbs: drop る (ru) and add させる (saseru).
For godan (u-) verbs: change the last vowel to the あ (a) column and add せる (seru).

Example from this song:
誰にも邪魔させるワケにはいかない (dare ni mo jama saseru wake ni wa ikanai, "I cannot let anyone interfere")

More examples:
- 子供を遊ばせる (kodomo o asobaseru, "to let the child play")
- 食べさせる (tabesaseru, "to make/let someone eat")
- 先生が学生に本を読ませた (sensei ga gakusei ni hon o yomaseta, "The teacher made the students read a book")

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 邪魔する (jama suru) → 邪魔させる (jama saseru, causative)

grammar_points.name: 〜てあげる (te ageru - do for someone)

explanation.en:
Expresses doing something as a favor for someone else. It adds a "giving" nuance to the action, meaning "I will do [this] for you."

How it works:
Take the て-form (te-form) of a verb and add あげる (ageru). The subject does the action for the benefit of another person.

Example from this song:
いつか僕が見せてあげる光り輝く世界を (itsuka boku ga misete ageru hikari kagayaku sekai o, "Someday I will show you a brilliantly shining world")

More examples:
- 教えてあげる (oshiete ageru, "I will teach you")
- 手伝ってあげた (tetsudatte ageta, "I helped them out")
- 作ってあげよう (tsukutte ageyou, "Let me make it for you")

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 見せる (miseru) → 見せて (misete) → 見せてあげる (misete ageru)

grammar_points.name: 〜合う (au - mutual/reciprocal action)

explanation.en:
When attached to a verb stem, 合う (au) indicates that two or more people do an action to/for each other. It turns a one-way action into a mutual, reciprocal one.

How it works:
Take the masu-stem of a verb (remove ます) and add 合う (au). This creates a compound verb meaning "do X together/to each other."

Example from this song:
交わし合った革命の契り (kawashi atta kakumei no chigiri, "The revolutionary oath we exchanged together")

More examples:
- 助け合う (tasuke au, "to help each other")
- 話し合う (hanashi au, "to discuss together")
- 愛し合う (aishi au, "to love each other")

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 交わす (kawasu) → 交わし (kawashi, masu-stem) + 合う (au) → 交わし合う (kawashi au)

explanation.en: Noun + めく forms a verb meaning 'to take on the feel/aspect of X'. Past form 〜めいた modifies a noun: 奇跡めいた妄想 'a delusion tinged with miracle'. More poetic than 〜のような ('like X'). Common pairings: 春めく ('spring-like'), 謎めいた ('mysterious').
explanation.es: Sustantivo + めく forma un verbo: 'tomar el cariz de X'. Forma pasada 〜めいた modifica sustantivo: 奇跡めいた妄想 'fantasía con tono de milagro'. Más poético que 〜のような. Frecuentes: 春めく, 謎めいた.
explanation.pt-BR: Substantivo + めく forma um verbo que significa 'tomar o aspecto de X'. Forma passada 〜めいた modifica substantivo: 奇跡めいた妄想 'fantasia com tom de milagre'. Mais poético que 〜のような. Comuns: 春めく, 謎めいた.

explanation.en: Negative verb stem + ないで is a softer 'don't' / 'please don't' than the imperative. 満たさないで '(please) don't fill it', 鳴らさないで '(please) don't sound it'. Often used in songs and emotional pleas.
explanation.es: Raíz negativa del verbo + ないで es un 'no hagas' más suave que el imperativo. 満たさないで '(por favor) no llenes', 鳴らさないで '(por favor) no hagas sonar'. Común en letras y súplicas.
explanation.pt-BR: Radical negativo do verbo + ないで é um 'não faça' mais suave que o imperativo. 満たさないで '(por favor) não preencha', 鳴らさないで '(por favor) não toque'. Comum em letras e súplicas emocionais.

explanation.en: Verb stem + 続ける ('to continue') means 'keep doing X / continue X-ing'. 壊し続けた '(I) kept breaking', 走り続ける 'keep running'. Often combined with past form to describe a long-running, often regrettable action.
explanation.es: Raíz del verbo + 続ける significa 'seguir haciendo X'. 壊し続けた '(yo) seguí rompiendo', 走り続ける 'seguir corriendo'. A menudo en pasado para acciones prolongadas y a veces lamentables.
explanation.pt-BR: Radical do verbo + 続ける significa 'continuar fazendo X'. 壊し続けた '(eu) continuei quebrando', 走り続ける 'continuar correndo'. Frequente no passado para ações prolongadas e às vezes lamentáveis.

grammar_points.name: 〜ように (in the way of, as if)

explanation.en: Verb (plain) + ように compares manner: 'as if / in the way that'. 囁くように刺して 'pierce me as a whisper would'; ほどけるように 'as if coming undone'. Distinct from 〜ように meaning 'so that' (purpose).
explanation.es: Verbo (forma simple) + ように compara modo: 'como si / del modo en que'. 囁くように刺して 'atraviésame como un susurro'; ほどけるように 'como si fuera a deshacerse'.
explanation.pt-BR: Verbo (forma simples) + ように compara modo: 'como se / da forma como'. 囁くように刺して 'atravesse como um sussurro'; ほどけるように 'como se fosse se desfazer'.

explanation.en: Verb te-form + しまう ('to put away') = 'do completely / end up doing (regrettably)'. 残されてしまった = 'we ended up being left behind' (with regret). Often shortened to 〜ちゃう / 〜ちゃった in casual speech.
explanation.es: Forma -te del verbo + しまう ('guardar') = 'hacer del todo / terminar haciendo (con pena)'. 残されてしまった = 'acabamos quedándonos'. Casual: 〜ちゃう / 〜ちゃった.
explanation.pt-BR: Forma -te do verbo + しまう ('guardar') = 'fazer por completo / acabar fazendo (lamentavelmente)'. 残されてしまった = 'acabamos sendo deixados'. Casual: 〜ちゃう / 〜ちゃった.

explanation.en: Group-2 verb stem + よ is the classical imperative — 与える → 与えよ ('grant!'), 信ぜよ ('believe!'). Solemn or biblical register, distinct from modern 与えろ. Used in songs, prayers, formal commands. The matching Group-1 form is just verb-e (走れ).
explanation.es: Raíz del verbo Grupo 2 + よ es el imperativo clásico — 与える → 与えよ ('¡concede!'), 信ぜよ ('¡cree!'). Registro solemne o bíblico, distinto del moderno 与えろ. Usado en letras, plegarias, órdenes formales.
explanation.pt-BR: Radical do verbo Grupo 2 + よ é o imperativo clássico — 与える → 与えよ ('conceda!'), 信ぜよ ('creia!'). Registro solene ou bíblico, distinto do moderno 与えろ. Usado em letras, orações, ordens formais.

grammar_points.name: 〜ならば (naraba: if)

explanation.en:
How it works: Add ならば (naraba) after a noun or clause to express a formal or literary conditional — 'if it is X' or 'if that's the case'. It's the formal version of なら (nara).

Example from this song: 太陽ならば (taiyou naraba) = 'if it were the sun / if I were the sun' — from 太陽 (taiyou, 'sun') + ならば (naraba, 'if')

More examples:
• 君 (kimi, 'you') → 君ならば (kimi naraba, 'if it's you')
• 本当 (hontou, 'true') → 本当ならば (hontou naraba, 'if it's true')
• 愛 (ai, 'love') → 愛ならば (ai naraba, 'if it is love')

Note: Formality: ならば (most formal) > なら (standard) > だったら (most casual). ならば is common in songs, poetry, and dramatic speech. It sets up profound hypothetical scenarios.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 太陽 (taiyou, 'sun') + ならば (naraba, 'if') → 太陽ならば (taiyou naraba, 'if it were the sun')

grammar_points.name: 〜てきた (te kita: have been doing)

explanation.en:
How it works: Add てきた (te kita) after the te-form of a verb to express an action that has continued from the past up to now — 'have been doing X all along'.

Example from this song: 受け止めてきた (uketomete kita) = 'have been accepting/catching' — from 受け止める (uketomeru, 'to accept/catch') → 受け止めて (uketomete, te-form) + きた (kita, 'came'). Also: 抱えてきた (kakaete kita) = 'have been carrying/holding'

More examples:
• 戦う (tatakau, 'to fight') → 戦ってきた (tatakatte kita, 'have been fighting')
• 耐える (taeru, 'to endure') → 耐えてきた (taete kita, 'have been enduring')
• 愛する (ai suru, 'to love') → 愛してきた (ai shite kita, 'have been loving')

Note: てきた is deeply emotional in songs — it acknowledges accumulated experience and effort. 'All this time, through everything, I have been...' The song uses it twice, showing a pattern of enduring love.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 受け止める (uketomeru, 'to accept') → 受け止めて (uketomete, te-form) + きた (kita, 'came') → 受け止めてきた (uketomete kita, 'have been accepting')

grammar_points.name: 〜たら (tara: if; when)

explanation.en:
How it works: Add たら (tara) to the past form of a verb for a conditional — 'if/when X happens'. This song also uses the related form たなら (ta nara) for a more literary feel.

Example from this song: 感じられたら (kanjiraretara) = 'if I could feel' — from 感じられる (kanjirareru, potential of 感じる, 'to feel') → 感じられたら (kanjiraretara). Also: 癒せたなら (iyaseta nara) = 'if I could heal'

More examples:
• できる (dekiru, 'can do') → できたら (dekitara, 'if I could')
• 会える (aeru, 'can meet') → 会えたら (aetara, 'if we could meet')
• 届く (todoku, 'to reach') → 届いたら (todoitara, 'if/when it reaches')

Note: たら with potential verbs creates deeply wishful expressions: 'if only I could...' たなら is a more literary variant with the same meaning, perfect for song lyrics.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 感じられる (kanjirareru, 'can feel') → 感じられたら (kanjiraretara, 'if I could feel') / 癒せる (iyaseru, 'can heal') → 癒せたなら (iyaseta nara, 'if I could heal')

grammar_points.name: 〜さえ (sae: even)

explanation.en:
How it works: Add さえ (sae) after a noun or verb to mean 'even X' — emphasizing that the stated minimum is extreme or significant.

Example from this song: 泣くことさえ出来なかった (naku koto sae dekinakatta) = 'couldn't even cry' — from 泣く (naku, 'to cry') + こと (koto, nominalizer) + さえ (sae, 'even') + 出来なかった (dekinakatta, 'couldn't')

More examples:
• 名前 (namae, 'name') → 名前さえ知らない (namae sae shiranai, 'don't even know the name')
• 立つ (tatsu, 'to stand') → 立つことさえ (tatsu koto sae, 'even standing')
• 一言 (hitokoto, 'one word') → 一言さえ (hitokoto sae, 'even one word')

Note: さえ...ない expresses 'can't even do the minimum'. さえ...ば means 'as long as': 君さえいれば (kimi sae ireba, 'as long as you're here'). Context determines which meaning.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 泣く (naku, 'to cry') + こと (koto) + さえ (sae, 'even') + 出来なかった (dekinakatta, 'couldn't') → 泣くことさえ出来なかった (naku koto sae dekinakatta, 'couldn't even cry')

grammar_points.name: 〜てくれる (te kureru: to do for me)

explanation.en:
How it works: Add てくれる (te kureru) after the te-form of a verb to express that someone did something for the speaker's benefit — carrying gratitude and warmth.

Example from this song: 笑いかけてくれた (waraikakete kureta) = 'smiled at me (and I'm grateful)' — from 笑いかける (waraikakeru, 'to smile at') → 笑いかけて (waraikakete, te-form) + くれた (kureta, past of kureru, 'did for me')

More examples:
• 助ける (tasukeru, 'to help') → 助けてくれた (tasukete kureta, 'helped me')
• 来る (kuru, 'to come') → 来てくれた (kite kureta, 'came for me')
• 信じる (shinjiru, 'to believe') → 信じてくれた (shinjite kureta, 'believed in me')

Note: てくれる is one of the most emotionally significant patterns in Japanese. It transforms a neutral action into a gift — the person did something that benefited you, and you appreciate it. Essential for expressing gratitude in natural Japanese.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 笑いかける (waraikakeru, 'to smile at') → 笑いかけて (waraikakete, te-form) + くれた (kureta, 'did for me') → 笑いかけてくれた (waraikakete kureta, 'smiled at me')

grammar_points.name: 〜ではなくて (de wa nakute: not X, but)

explanation.en:
How it works: Use noun + ではなくて (de wa nakute) or the casual じゃなくて (ja nakute) to negate one thing and introduce another — 'not X, but rather Y'.

Example from this song: 景色じゃなくて (keshiki ja nakute) = 'not the scenery, but...' — from 景色 (keshiki, 'scenery') + じゃなくて (ja nakute, 'not, but') → followed by 眩しさを (mabushisa wo, 'the brightness')

More examples:
• 嘘 (uso, 'lie') → 嘘じゃなくて本当 (uso ja nakute hontou, 'not a lie, but the truth')
• お金 (okane, 'money') → お金じゃなくて時間 (okane ja nakute jikan, 'not money, but time')
• 悲しい (kanashii, 'sad') → 悲しいんじゃなくて寂しい (kanashii n ja nakute sabishii, 'not sad, but lonely')

Note: じゃなくて is casual; ではなくて is formal. This pattern clarifies what you really mean — correcting a possible misunderstanding. Very useful in daily conversation.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 景色 (keshiki, 'scenery') + じゃなくて (ja nakute, 'not, but') → 景色じゃなくて (keshiki ja nakute, 'not the scenery, but...') + 眩しさを (mabushisa wo, 'the brightness')

explanation.en: Attaches to a verb's -e- stem to mean 'if/when X.' Used for hypotheticals, natural consequences, and reflective statements: 思い出せば 'when I think back'.
explanation.es: Se adjunta a la raíz -e- del verbo para significar 'si/cuando X'. Usada para hipótesis, consecuencias naturales y reflexiones: 思い出せば 'cuando recuerdo'.
explanation.pt-BR: Anexa-se ao radical -e- do verbo para significar 'se/quando X'. Usada para hipóteses, consequências naturais e reflexões: 思い出せば 'quando me lembro'.

explanation.en: 〜ていた describes an ongoing past state or action. In casual speech and lyrics it contracts to 〜てた: 輝いてた = 'was shining', 眠っていた = 'was sleeping'.
explanation.es: 〜ていた describe un estado o acción continuos en el pasado. En el habla casual y las letras se contrae a 〜てた: 輝いてた = 'estaba brillando', 眠っていた = 'estábamos durmiendo'.
explanation.pt-BR: 〜ていた descreve um estado ou ação contínuos no passado. Na fala casual e em letras contrai-se para 〜てた: 輝いてた = 'estava brilhando', 眠っていた = 'estávamos dormindo'.

grammar_points.name: 〜たい / 〜たくなる (desire and emerging desire)

explanation.en: 〜たい (attached to verb stem) means 'want to'. 〜たくなる ('come to want to') describes a desire that arises naturally over time: 疑いたくなる 'I start wanting to doubt'. With 〜ていたい you keep wanting an ongoing state — 見ていたい 'want to keep watching'.
explanation.es: 〜たい (a la raíz verbal) significa 'querer'. 〜たくなる ('llegar a querer') describe un deseo que surge con el tiempo: 疑いたくなる 'empiezo a querer dudar'. Con 〜ていたい uno quiere continuar un estado: 見ていたい 'quiero seguir mirando'.
explanation.pt-BR: 〜たい (anexado ao radical do verbo) significa 'querer'. 〜たくなる ('vir a querer') descreve um desejo que surge naturalmente: 疑いたくなる 'começo a querer duvidar'. Com 〜ていたい você quer continuar um estado: 見ていたい 'quero continuar olhando'.

explanation.en: Plain form + そうだ means 'I hear that...' / 'they say...' — reporting information from someone else. Distinct from the look-like 〜そう that attaches to verb/adjective stems.
explanation.es: Forma simple + そうだ significa 'he oído que...' / 'dicen que...' — informando algo que se ha oído. Distinto del 〜そう de apariencia que se adjunta a la raíz.
explanation.pt-BR: Forma simples + そうだ significa 'ouvi dizer que...' / 'dizem que...' — relatando informação de outra pessoa. Diferente do 〜そう de aparência que se anexa ao radical.

explanation.en: An archaic equivalent of 〜ない still found in poetry, set phrases, and song lyrics for solemn or formal weight: 会えぬ人 'a person I cannot meet', 行かぬ 'does not go'. Attaches like 〜ない (to verb a-stem; する → せぬ; くる → こぬ).
explanation.es: Un equivalente arcaico de 〜ない aún presente en poesía, frases hechas y letras de canciones, con tono solemne: 会えぬ人 'persona a la que no puedo encontrar'. Se adjunta como 〜ない (raíz -a; する → せぬ; くる → こぬ).
explanation.pt-BR: Um equivalente arcaico de 〜ない ainda usado em poesia, expressões fixas e letras de música para dar peso solene: 会えぬ人 'pessoa que não posso encontrar'. Anexa-se como 〜ない (radical -a; する → せぬ; くる → こぬ).

explanation.en: Plain verb/adjective + の at the end of a sentence gives a soft, often feminine, intimate explanation or assertion. Common in introspective lyrics: 忘れられなかったの 'I was never able to forget'. Distinct from explanatory んだ, which is more neutral.
explanation.es: Forma simple + の al final da una afirmación suave e íntima, con frecuencia femenina. Común en letras introspectivas: 忘れられなかったの 'nunca pude olvidar'. Diferente de んだ explicativo, que es más neutro.
explanation.pt-BR: Forma simples + の no final da frase dá uma asserção suave e íntima, frequentemente feminina. Comum em letras introspectivas: 忘れられなかったの 'nunca consegui esquecer'. Diferente de んだ explicativo, que é mais neutro.

grammar_points.name: 〜くらいなら (kurai nara: rather than)

explanation.en:
How it works: くらいなら (kurai nara) means 'rather than (doing X)' — it expresses that the speaker would prefer an extreme alternative over the stated option.

Example from this song: 殺られるくらいなら (yarareru kurai nara) = 'rather than being killed/beaten' — from 殺られる (yarareru, 'to be done in/killed', passive) + くらいなら

More examples:
• 負けるくらいなら死んだ方がいい (makeru kurai nara shinda hou ga ii, 'I'd rather die than lose')
• 嘘をつくくらいなら黙る (uso o tsuku kurai nara damaru, 'rather than lie, I'll stay quiet')
• 待つくらいなら自分でやる (matsu kurai nara jibun de yaru, 'rather than wait, I'll do it myself')

Note: くらいなら literally means 'if it's to the extent of...' — the speaker finds the stated action so unacceptable that they'd prefer an alternative. It's dramatic and emphatic.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 殺られる (yarareru, 'to be beaten') + くらいなら (kurai nara, 'rather than') → 殺られるくらいなら (yarareru kurai nara, 'rather than be beaten')

grammar_points.name: 〜すぎる (sugiru: too much)

explanation.en:
How it works: すぎる (sugiru, 'to exceed') attaches to verb stems or adjective stems to express 'too much.' For verbs: masu-stem + すぎる. For i-adjectives: drop い + すぎる.

Example from this song: 若すぎる (wakasugiru) = 'too young' — from 若い (wakai, 'young') → 若 (waka) + すぎる (sugiru)

More examples:
• 食べすぎる (tabesugiru, 'to eat too much') — from 食べる (taberu, 'to eat')
• 高すぎる (takasugiru, 'too expensive') — from 高い (takai, 'expensive')
• 静かすぎる (shizuka sugiru, 'too quiet') — na-adjective + すぎる

Note: すぎる conjugates as an ichidan verb: すぎた (sugita, past), すぎない (suginai, negative). This is one of the most frequently used grammar patterns — 暑すぎる！(atsusugiru, 'it's too hot!').

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 若い (wakai, 'young') → 若 (waka, drop い) + すぎる (sugiru, 'too much') → 若すぎる (wakasugiru, 'too young')

grammar_points.name: 〜なよ (na yo: don't do!)

explanation.en:
How it works: な (na) after a verb's dictionary form is a casual negative command: 'don't do X!' Adding よ (yo) makes it slightly softer or more emphatic depending on tone.

Example from this song: 隠すなよ (kakusu na yo) = 'don't hide it!' — from 隠す (kakusu, 'to hide') + な (na, 'don't') + よ (yo)

More examples:
• 泣くな (naku na, 'don't cry!') — from 泣く (naku, 'to cry')
• 心配するなよ (shinpai suru na yo, 'don't worry!') — from 心配する (shinpai suru, 'to worry')
• 諦めるな (akirameru na, 'don't give up!') — from 諦める (akirameru, 'to give up')

Note: Dictionary form + な is the rough masculine prohibition form. It's very common in anime and songs. Don't confuse with the な that makes na-adjectives (静かな = quiet).

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 隠す (kakusu, 'to hide') + な (na, 'don't') + よ (yo, emphasis) → 隠すなよ (kakusu na yo, 'don't hide it!')

grammar_points.name: 〜にだって (ni datte: even by)

explanation.en:
How it works: にだって (ni datte) combines に (ni, 'by') with だって (datte, 'even'). It emphasizes that even the stated agent or means can or can't do something.

Example from this song: テロリストにだって消せない (terorisuto ni datte kesenai) = 'even a terrorist can't erase it' — emphasizing that not even the most extreme agent can destroy it

More examples:
• 誰にだって秘密がある (dare ni datte himitsu ga aru, 'even anyone has secrets / everyone has secrets')
• 子供にだってわかる (kodomo ni datte wakaru, 'even a child can understand')
• 親にだって言えない (oya ni datte ienai, 'can't tell even my parents')

Note: だって adds the nuance of 'even.' It's more emphatic than でも. にだって specifically emphasizes 'even by (this agent).' It's a punk/rebellious way to make a strong point.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: テロリスト (terorisuto, 'terrorist') + に (ni, 'by') + だって (datte, 'even') → テロリストにだって (terorisuto ni datte, 'even by a terrorist') + 消せない (kesenai, 'can't erase')

grammar_points.name: 〜てくれ (te kure: do it for me! / please do)

explanation.en:
How it works: くれ (kure) is the imperative of くれる (kureru, 'to do for me'). Attach it to a verb's te-form for a rough/casual request: 'do this for me!'

Example from this song: 聞いてくれ (kiite kure) = 'listen to me!' — from 聞く (kiku, 'to listen') → 聞いて (kiite) + くれ (kure)

More examples:
• 見てくれ (mite kure, 'look at this!') — from 見る (miru, 'to see')
• 信じてくれ (shinjite kure, 'believe me!') — from 信じる (shinjiru, 'to believe')
• 待ってくれ (matte kure, 'wait for me!') — from 待つ (matsu, 'to wait')

Note: てくれ is more direct/rough than てください. It's masculine and common in punk, rock, and emotional contexts. Adding よ softens it slightly: 聞いてくれよ (kiite kure yo).

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 聞く (kiku, 'to listen') → 聞いて (kiite) → 聞いてくれ (kiite kure, 'listen to me!')

grammar_points.name: 〜じまう (jimau: end up doing)

explanation.en:
How it works: じまう (jimau) is the rough casual contraction of でしまう (de shimau). It expresses unintended or regrettable completion. Used after verbs whose te-form ends in で.

Example from this song: 死んじまう (shinjimau) = 'end up dying' — from 死ぬ (shinu, 'to die') → 死んで (shinde) + しまう (shimau) → contracted: 死んじまう (shinjimau)

More examples:
• 飲んじまった (nonjimatta, 'ended up drinking it') — from 飲む (nomu, 'to drink')
• 壊れちまう (kowarechimau, 'gonna end up breaking') — from 壊れる (kowareru, 'to break')
• やっちまった (yacchimatta, 'I messed up / did it') — from やる (yaru, 'to do')

Note: The contraction pattern: てしまう → ちまう/ちゃう, でしまう → じまう/じゃう. じまう is rougher and more masculine than じゃう. Very common in punk/rock lyrics.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 死ぬ (shinu, 'to die') → 死んで (shinde) + しまう (shimau) → 死んじまう (shinjimau, 'end up dying')

explanation.en:
A conditional meaning "if." Used when the speaker takes a hypothetical situation as a premise, then states what would follow.

How it works:
Attach なら (nara) after the plain form of a verb, adjective, or noun.

Example from this song:
あの頃に戻れるなら (ano koro ni modoreru nara, "If we could return to those days")

More examples:
- 時間があるなら手伝って (jikan ga aru nara tetsudatte, "If you have time, help me")
- 安いなら買う (yasui nara kau, "If it’s cheap, I’ll buy it")
- 行くなら早く行こう (iku nara hayaku ikou, "If we’re going, let’s go quickly")

Creates a comparison: "like" or "as if." It connects a descriptive phrase to a noun, saying one thing resembles another.

How it works:
Place ような (you na) after a noun + の (no), or after a verb in dictionary form.

Example from this song:
ガラス細工のような思い出の破片 (garasu saiku no you na omoide no hahen, "Fragments of memories like glasswork")

More examples:
- 夢のような話 (yume no you na hanashi, "A story like a dream")
- 子供のように笑う (kodomo no you ni warau, "Laugh like a child")
- 嵐のような日々 (arashi no you na hibi, "Days like a storm")

Indicates a sequence: "after doing [X], then [Y]." The first action must be completed before the second begins.

How it works:
Take the て-form (te-form) of a verb and add から (kara).

Example from this song:
失くしてから気づく (nakushite kara kidzuku, "You realize after losing")

More examples:
- ご飯を食べてから出かける (gohan o tabete kara dekakeru, "Go out after eating")
- 日本に来てから日本語を勉強した (nihon ni kite kara nihongo o benkyou shita, "Studied Japanese after coming to Japan")
- 話してから決めよう (hanashite kara kimeyou, "Decide after talking")

An emphatic particle meaning "even." It highlights an extreme or unexpected example, implying "if even [this] is the case, then certainly everything else too."

How it works:
Place さえ (sae) after a noun, or after verb + ことさえ. Often paired with も (mo) for extra emphasis.

Example from this song:
夢見ることさえも叶わず (yumemiru koto sae mo kanawazu, "Unable to even dream")

More examples:
- 名前さえ知らない (namae sae shiranai, "I don’t even know their name")
- 水さえあれば生きられる (mizu sae areba ikirareru, "If we just have water, we can survive")
- 子供でさえ分かる (kodomo de sae wakaru, "Even a child can understand")

Defines or names something. It connects a description or name to a noun, meaning "called," "known as," or "the thing that is."

How it works:
Place という (to iu) between a name/description and the noun it modifies.

Example from this song:
現実という鎖 (genjitsu to iu kusari, "The chains called reality")

More examples:
- 東京という街 (toukyou to iu machi, "The city called Tokyo")
- 愛という名の病 (ai to iu na no yamai, "An illness called love")
- 自由という概念 (jiyuu to iu gainen, "The concept known as freedom")

grammar_points.name: 〜てもいい (temo ii - it’s okay to)

explanation.en:
Expresses permission or willingness: "it’s okay to [do X]" or "I don’t mind if [X]." The speaker accepts the action described.

How it works:
Take the て-form (te-form) of a verb and add もいい (mo ii).

Example from this song:
すべてを犠牲にしてもいい (subete o gisei ni shite mo ii, "It’s fine to sacrifice everything")

More examples:
- ここに座ってもいいですか (koko ni suwatte mo ii desu ka, "May I sit here?")
- 食べてもいいよ (tabete mo ii yo, "You can eat it")
- 遅れてもいいから来て (okurete mo ii kara kite, "It’s okay to be late, just come")

translations.en: Here I come! Certain victory! Strongest in history!
translations.es: ¡He llegado! ¡Victoria asegurada! ¡El más fuerte de la historia!
translations.pt-BR: Cheguei! Vitória certa! O mais forte da história!

literal_meaning.en: Have-arrived! Certain-win! History-strongest!

cultural_context.en: 参上 ('san-jou') is the humble verb 'to arrive (before someone of higher rank).' Used here ironically as a battle cry — Saitama announcing himself as an underling-style entry. 史上最強 packs four kanji into 'strongest in all of history.'

translations.en: What's your problem?! Frustration! I don't stop!
translations.es: ¿Cuál es el problema?! ¡Frustración! ¡Yo no paro!
translations.pt-BR: Qual é a desse?! Frustração! Eu não paro!

literal_meaning.en: What is-it-saying! Frustration! I as-for, won't-stop!

cultural_context.en: 何だってんだ contracts 何だと言っているんだ ('what are you saying?'). Sounds growled. 俺 (ore) is rough masculine 'I' — a register choice that picks a fight before any verb arrives.

translations.en: ONE PUNCH! Done! Win after win!
translations.es: ONE PUNCH! ¡Completado! ¡Victorias en cadena!
translations.pt-BR: ONE PUNCH! Concluído! Vitórias em cadeia!

literal_meaning.en: One-punch, completed, consecutive-battles consecutive-wins

cultural_context.en: 連戦連勝 ('battle-after-battle, win-after-win') doubles the same construction (連〜連〜) for the militaristic feel of unbroken streaks. Common pattern: 連〜連〜 = 'X after X.'

translations.en: I am a war cry! I always win! Crushing victory!
translations.es: ¡Yo soy el grito de guerra! ¡Siempre gano! ¡Victoria aplastante!
translations.pt-BR: Eu sou o grito de guerra! Sempre venço! Vitória esmagadora!

literal_meaning.en: I as-for, KATSU! always win, crushing-victory

cultural_context.en: 喝 (katsu!) is the Zen master's shout used to break a student's mental block — yelling-as-teaching. Punning trick: 喝 (katsu shout) and 勝つ (katsu, to win) are homophones, so '俺は喝!' reads simultaneously as 'I am the shout' and 'I win.'

translations.en: Right up to the very limit
translations.es: Justo hasta el mismo límite
translations.pt-BR: Bem no limite, no limite

literal_meaning.en: Right-at-edge limit until

cultural_context.en: ギリギリ — onomatopoeia for 'just barely / right at the edge.' Stacked with 限界 ('limit'), it doubles the 'on the brink' feeling.

translations.en: Voices that praise me, applause and the like — I don't want any of it
translations.es: Voces que me elogian, ovaciones y demás — no las quiero, ¿eh?
translations.pt-BR: Vozes que me elogiam, ovação e essas coisas — não quero, viu

literal_meaning.en: Me (obj) praising voice or-such, applause-something-like, want-as-for-not-ze

cultural_context.en: 讃える ('to praise / extol' — written 称える or 賛える as well) is a more elevated word than 褒める ('praise'). The casual 〜なんて dismisses the listed items as unworthy. ぜ at sentence end is rough masculine emphasis — 'I'm telling you.'

translations.en: That's why I strike down evil where no one sees
translations.es: Por eso golpeo al mal sin que nadie me vea
translations.pt-BR: Por isso bato no mal sem ninguém ver

literal_meaning.en: So, person-not-knowing evil (obj) strike

cultural_context.en: 人知れず ('without people knowing' — bungo-style negative) is literary cousin of modern 人に知られないで. The kanji 人 acts as 'people' generally. This is Saitama's whole drama: he saves the world but stays invisible.

translations.en: Enemies pressing in, blanketing the sky — I will not turn my back
translations.es: Enemigos avanzando, tapando el cielo — no voy a darles la espalda
translations.pt-BR: Inimigos avançando, cobrindo o céu — não vou virar as costas

literal_meaning.en: Sky covering surge enemies, I as-for back (obj) turn-as-for-not-do

cultural_context.en: 天 normally read てん, here read そら ('sky') as a furigana stylization — kanji says 'heaven,' voice says 'sky.' 押し寄せる ('press-in-and-approach') is the verb for waves crashing or armies surging. The split-verb negation 向けはしない is emphatic refusal: 'turn? — that I will NOT do.'

translations.en: If I am a hero, I have forged an unshakable resolve — unleash the iron fist!
translations.es: Si soy un héroe, he forjado una resolución inquebrantable — ¡desata el puño de hierro!
translations.pt-BR: Se sou um herói, fixei uma resolução inabalável — desencadeia o punho de ferro!

literal_meaning.en: Hero if-be, unshakable-no resolve forged, unleash-imp. iron-fist

cultural_context.en: 揺ぎなき = 揺るぎ ('shaking, stem of 揺るぐ') + なき (literary 'no / without') = 'no-shaking,' modifying 覚悟. The 〜き / 〜なき endings are bungo (classical) attributive forms — modern equivalents are 〜い / 〜ない.

translations.en: Here I come! Go on! Fair and square!
translations.es: ¡Aquí estoy! ¡Go on! ¡Limpio y honesto!
translations.pt-BR: Cheguei! Go on! Limpo e honesto!

literal_meaning.en: Have-arrived! Go on! Right-right-noble-noble

cultural_context.en: 正々堂々 ('right-right-noble-noble') = 'with full integrity, no underhanded tricks.' Sports-anime staple yojijukugo. The doubling for emphasis (X-X-Y-Y) is a common four-character structure.

translations.en: What's the deal? I don't feel a thing. Ain't no enemies left
translations.es: ¿Qué pasa? No siento nada. Ya no quedan enemigos
translations.pt-BR: Mas que história é essa? Não sinto nada. Não tem mais inimigo

literal_meaning.en: How is-becoming-it-is? Nothing feel-not, no-longer enemy is-not

cultural_context.en: 感じねぇ = 感じない slurred to ねぇ. 居ねぇ = 居ない slurred. Rough masculine register replaces -ai endings with -ee — heard in shounen anime, yakuza films, and tough-guy speech. Captures Saitama's bored disappointment perfectly.

translations.en: JUSTICE! Execute! No discussion!
translations.es: ¡JUSTICE! ¡Ejecutar! ¡Sin discusión!
translations.pt-BR: JUSTICE! Em execução! Sem conversa!

literal_meaning.en: Justice, execute, question-answer-no-need

cultural_context.en: 問答無用 ('Q&A useless') = 'no point arguing, action time.' Used by samurai-era authority figures and modern action heroes alike to shut down debate before a fight.

translations.en: I win! Sever evil! Hands together — a prayer for the dead
translations.es: ¡Yo gano! ¡Corto el mal! ¡Manos juntas — descansen en paz!
translations.pt-BR: Eu venço! Corto o mal! Mãos juntas — paz aos defuntos

literal_meaning.en: I (subj) win, evil (obj) sever, hands-together

cultural_context.en: 合掌 ('hands together') is the Buddhist gesture of prayer or thanks — placed at the end of a ritual, often in funerals. Saying 合掌 over a defeated enemy = 'rest in peace, bro.'

translations.en: Adrenaline overflowing — let it rip! Land the technique you trained!
translations.es: Adrenalina desbordándose — ¡suéltala! ¡Aplica la técnica entrenada!
translations.pt-BR: Adrenalina transbordando — solta tudo! Manda a técnica treinada!

literal_meaning.en: Adrenaline start-overflow-ze, trained technique (obj) ram-imp.

cultural_context.en: ブチかます is slang from boxing/sumo — 'land a hit so hard it overwhelms.' Imperative 〜かませ adds the urgency. 鍛える ('to forge / train,' as a blade is forged) frames the body as a weapon.

translations.en: No matter how strong a guy is — they were once just a tiny kid
translations.es: Por más fuerte que sea un tipo — alguna vez fue un mocoso pequeño
translations.pt-BR: Não importa quão forte seja o cara — todos foram pirralhos

literal_meaning.en: However-much strong guy-also, tiny brat was-it-is

cultural_context.en: ちっぽけ (chippoke) ='tiny / insignificant,' a casual expressive word. ガキ (gaki) is rough slang for 'kid/brat' — registers don't get more masculine-rough. やつ ('guy / dude') matches the energy.

translations.en: Hero — overcoming the weak self, becoming strong
translations.es: Héroe — superando al yo débil, haciéndose fuerte
translations.pt-BR: Herói — superando o eu fraco, tornando-se forte

literal_meaning.en: Weak-classical self, overcome, strong-become

cultural_context.en: 弱き is the bungo attributive form of 弱い ('weak') — modern: 弱い. 己 (onore) is the formal/literary 'self' (more elevated than 自分). Both choices push the line toward 'samurai-philosophy' register.

translations.en: Holding up a fist where a god dwells, I just charge forward
translations.es: Alzando un puño donde habita un dios, yo solo sigo adelante
translations.pt-BR: Erguendo o punho onde mora um deus, eu só sigo em frente

literal_meaning.en: God-dwell fist hoisting, I as-for, charge-only-sa

cultural_context.en: 神宿る ('god-dwells-in') is a literary attributive — verb directly modifying noun. 拳 (kobushi) is the more dignified word for 'fist' (vs. 拳骨 'genkotsu'). 掲げる ('to hoist a flag/banner') gives the fist banner-energy.

translations.en: A hero — fighting until the day he tastes the mud of defeat
translations.es: Un héroe — luchando hasta el día en que pruebe el barro de la derrota
translations.pt-BR: Um herói — lutando até o dia em que provar a lama da derrota

literal_meaning.en: Someday defeat-by mud lick until, fight

cultural_context.en: 汚泥を舐める ('to lick the filthy mud') = the idiom 'to taste defeat / to be humiliatingly beaten.' Saitama's whole arc is the search for this experience — he's bored with always winning. The verb-clause + まで construction means 'until the action happens.'

translations.en: I won't give up — drawing tomorrow on this chest
translations.es: No me rindo — dibujando el mañana en este pecho
translations.pt-BR: Eu não desisto — desenhando o amanhã neste peito

literal_meaning.en: I as-for, give-up-not, that chest-on future (obj) draw

cultural_context.en: 未来 normally read みらい, here read あす ('tomorrow') — a furigana stylization (kanji says 'future,' voice says 'tomorrow'). Singer Endoh Masaaki of JAM Project is famous for this kind of layered meaning.

translations.en: Toward an awakening world, now — soar! Strong and high!
translations.es: Hacia un mundo que despierta, ahora — ¡vuela! ¡Fuerte y alto!
translations.pt-BR: Rumo a um mundo que desperta, agora — voa! Forte e alto!

literal_meaning.en: Awakening-go world toward, now, soar-imp. strong high

cultural_context.en: 舞い上がる ('dance-rise' = soar / take wing) — combines 舞う ('dance') and 上がる ('rise'). The imperative 舞い上がれ commands the verb. 目覚めゆく uses the literary 〜ゆく for 〜いく.

translations.en: At any time — no matter what happens
translations.es: En cualquier momento — pase lo que pase
translations.pt-BR: Em qualquer hora — aconteça o que acontecer

literal_meaning.en: Any-kind-of time even, anything (subj) even-if-being

cultural_context.en: Stock duo of concessive clauses, parallel-built: どんな時でも (any-time-even) + 何があっても (anything-be-even-if). Together they cover 'every conceivable situation.'

tokens.romaji: I wanna be the SAIKYOU Hero
tokens.reading: アイワナビーザサイキョーヒーロー
tokens.surface: I wanna be the SAIKYOU Hero

translations.en: A lonely hero — I wanna be the SAIKYOU (strongest) Hero!
translations.es: Un héroe solitario — I wanna be the SAIKYOU (el más fuerte) Hero!
translations.pt-BR: Um herói solitário — I wanna be the SAIKYOU (mais forte) Hero!

literal_meaning.en: Lonely hero, I wanna be the strongest hero

cultural_context.en: 孤独 (kodoku) is the song's quietest beat — the cost of strength is loneliness. The closing line code-switches into English with 最強 SAIKYOU dropped in untranslated, leaving the strongest word in Japanese exactly where it lands hardest.

meaning.es: el más fuerte de la historia

explanation.en: Compounds inherited from classical Chinese — fixed four-kanji units where each character contributes meaning. JAM Project leans hard on battle yojijukugo: 史上最強 ('history-on strongest' = strongest ever), 連戦連勝 ('consecutive-battle consecutive-win' = winning streak), 正々堂々 ('right-right noble-noble' = fair and square), 問答無用 ('Q&A useless' = no discussion), 圧勝 ('press-win' = crushing victory — two characters, but same construction). Common doubled patterns: X-X-Y-Y (正々堂々), X-A-X-B (連戦連勝), and antonym pairs (問答無用 sets question and answer as a unit, then dismisses it). Memorize as units, not character by character.
explanation.es: Compuestos heredados del chino clásico — unidades fijas de cuatro kanji donde cada carácter aporta significado. JAM Project se apoya en yojijukugo de batalla: 史上最強 ('en la historia, el más fuerte'), 連戦連勝 ('batallas en cadena, victorias en cadena'), 正々堂々 ('limpio y honesto'), 問答無用 ('sin preguntas, sin discusión'), 圧勝 ('victoria aplastante' — solo dos kanji, misma lógica). Patrones comunes: X-X-Y-Y (正々堂々), X-A-X-B (連戦連勝), y pares antónimos (問答無用). Memoriza como unidades, no kanji por kanji.
explanation.pt-BR: Compostos herdados do chinês clássico — unidades fixas de quatro kanji onde cada caractere contribui significado. JAM Project se apoia em yojijukugo de batalha: 史上最強 ('na história, o mais forte'), 連戦連勝 ('batalhas seguidas, vitórias seguidas'), 正々堂々 ('limpo e honesto'), 問答無用 ('sem perguntas, sem discussão'), 圧勝 ('vitória esmagadora' — só dois kanji, mesma lógica). Padrões comuns: X-X-Y-Y (正々堂々), X-A-X-B (連戦連勝), e pares antônimos (問答無用). Memorize como unidades, não kanji por kanji.

explanation.en: Bare imperative for godlike orders. u-verbs replace final -u with -e: 繰り出す → 繰り出せ ('unleash!'), 舞い上がる → 舞い上がれ ('soar!'), ブチかます → ブチかませ ('land it!'). ru-verbs replace -ru with -ろ: 食べる → 食べろ. The form is blunt — too rough for everyday requests but standard for shounen battle dialogue, dog commands, and shouted instructions. Softer alternatives: 〜なさい (mom-voice), 〜てください (polite ask).
explanation.es: Imperativo puro para órdenes de dios. Verbos-u cambian -u final por -e: 繰り出す → 繰り出せ ('¡desencadena!'), 舞い上がる → 舞い上がれ ('¡vuela!'), ブチかます → ブチかませ ('¡suéltalo!'). Verbos-ru cambian -ru por -ろ: 食べる → 食べろ. La forma es áspera — demasiado ruda para el día a día, pero estándar para batalla shounen, órdenes a perros e instrucciones a gritos. Alternativas suaves: 〜なさい (voz de madre), 〜てください (petición cortés).
explanation.pt-BR: Imperativo puro para ordens de deus. Verbos-u trocam -u final por -e: 繰り出す → 繰り出せ ('desencadeia!'), 舞い上がる → 舞い上がれ ('voa!'), ブチかます → ブチかませ ('manda!'). Verbos-ru trocam -ru por -ろ: 食べる → 食べろ. A forma é seca — rude demais pro dia a dia, mas padrão pra batalha shounen, comando a cachorro e instrução berrada. Alternativas suaves: 〜なさい (voz de mãe), 〜てください (pedido educado).

grammar_points.name: Masculine register: 俺, ぜ, ねぇ contractions

explanation.en: Japanese encodes social register tightly into pronouns and sentence-final particles. 俺 (ore) is rough masculine 'I' — distinct from polite 私 (watashi) and softer 僕 (boku). Sentence-final ぜ adds masculine emphatic confidence ('I'm telling you'). The vowel shift -ai → -ee turns standard endings into rough/blue-collar speech: ない → ねぇ (感じない → 感じねぇ), 居ない → 居ねぇ. Heard everywhere in shounen anime, yakuza films, and Tokyo working-class speech.
explanation.es: El japonés codifica el registro social en los pronombres y partículas finales. 俺 (ore) es 'yo' masculino áspero — distinto del polite 私 (watashi) y el suave 僕 (boku). La partícula final ぜ añade énfasis masculino confiado. El cambio vocálico -ai → -ee convierte terminaciones estándar en habla áspera: ない → ねぇ (感じない → 感じねぇ), 居ない → 居ねぇ. Omnipresente en shounen, películas de yakuza y habla obrera de Tokio.
explanation.pt-BR: O japonês codifica registro social nos pronomes e partículas finais. 俺 (ore) é 'eu' masculino bruto — distinto do polido 私 (watashi) e do suave 僕 (boku). A partícula final ぜ adiciona ênfase masculina confiante. A mudança vocálica -ai → -ee transforma terminações padrão em fala bruta: ない → ねぇ (感じない → 感じねぇ), 居ない → 居ねぇ. Onipresente em shounen, filmes de yakuza e fala operária de Tóquio.

explanation.en: Particle attached to nouns or verb-dictionary forms to mean 'something like ~ / ~ and the like.' Distinctive feature: tone of dismissal or surprise. Listing X with なんて downgrades it: 喝采なんて欲しくはない ('applause and the like? — don't want it'). Compare neutral 喝采は欲しくない ('I don't want applause') vs scornful 喝采なんて欲しくない. Often pairs with surprised reaction: 'できるなんてすごい!' ('the fact that you can do it is amazing!').
explanation.es: Partícula unida a sustantivos o verbos en forma de diccionario con sentido 'algo como ~ / ~ y demás'. Marca: tono de desprecio o sorpresa. Listar X con なんて lo rebaja: 喝采なんて欲しくはない ('ovación y esas cosas — no la quiero'). Compara neutro 喝采は欲しくない vs. despectivo 喝采なんて欲しくない. Frecuente en reacción de sorpresa: 'できるなんてすごい!' ('¡que puedas hacerlo es increíble!').
explanation.pt-BR: Partícula ligada a substantivos ou verbos na forma de dicionário com sentido 'algo como ~ / ~ e tal'. Marca: tom de desdém ou surpresa. Listar X com なんて desvaloriza: 喝采なんて欲しくはない ('ovação e essas coisas? — não quero'). Compare neutro 喝采は欲しくない vs. desdenhoso 喝采なんて欲しくない. Frequente em reação surpresa: 'できるなんてすごい!' ('o fato de você conseguir é incrível!').

explanation.en: まで attaches not just to nouns ('until tomorrow') but also to whole verb-dictionary clauses to mean 'until V happens.' 敗北に汚泥舐めるまで = 'until I taste the mud of defeat.' The verb stays in the plain dictionary form before まで. Sets up an enduring action that won't stop until the V-clause becomes true.
explanation.es: まで se une no solo a sustantivos ('hasta mañana') sino a cláusulas enteras con verbo en forma de diccionario para 'hasta que V ocurra'. 敗北に汚泥舐めるまで = 'hasta que pruebe el barro de la derrota'. El verbo permanece en forma de diccionario antes de まで. Establece una acción prolongada que no se detiene hasta que la cláusula V se cumpla.
explanation.pt-BR: まで se liga não só a substantivos ('até amanhã') como a cláusulas inteiras de verbo na forma de dicionário com sentido 'até V acontecer'. 敗北に汚泥舐めるまで = 'até provar a lama da derrota'. O verbo fica na forma de dicionário antes de まで. Estabelece uma ação prolongada que não para até a cláusula V se tornar verdadeira.

explanation.en: Bungo (classical) attributive endings preserved in literary style. 〜き is the classical adjective attributive (modern 〜い): 弱き己 = 弱い己 ('weak self'). 〜なき is the literary 'without ~' or 'no ~' (modern 〜のない / 〜のない): 揺ぎなき覚悟 = 揺るぎのない覚悟 ('unshakable resolve'). Sprinkled into modern lyrics for samurai-style gravitas — using them everywhere would sound stilted, but a single 〜き or 〜なき per verse signals 'this is heroic register.'
explanation.es: Terminaciones atributivas del bungo (clásico) preservadas en estilo literario. 〜き es el atributivo clásico del adjetivo (moderno 〜い): 弱き己 = 弱い己. 〜なき es el 'sin ~' o 'no-~' literario (moderno 〜のない): 揺ぎなき覚悟 = 揺るぎのない覚悟 ('resolución inquebrantable'). Salpicados en letras modernas para gravitas samurái — usarlos siempre sonaría forzado, pero un 〜き o 〜なき por verso señala 'esto es registro heroico'.
explanation.pt-BR: Terminações atributivas do bungo (clássico) preservadas no estilo literário. 〜き é o atributivo clássico do adjetivo (moderno 〜い): 弱き己 = 弱い己. 〜なき é o 'sem ~' ou 'não-~' literário (moderno 〜のない): 揺ぎなき覚悟 = 揺るぎのない覚悟 ('resolução inabalável'). Salpicados na letra moderna pra peso de samurai — usar sempre soaria forçado, mas um 〜き ou 〜なき por verso sinaliza 'isto é registro heróico'.

synced_lrc.text: 揺れる陽炎 すべり出す汗
響きあう声 叩きあう肩

translations.en: Heat haze shimmers, sweat starts to slide
translations.es: Calina temblando, el sudor empieza a resbalar
translations.pt-BR: Miragem de calor tremula, o suor começa a escorrer

literal_meaning.en: Sway heat-haze, start-sliding sweat

cultural_context.en: 陽炎 (heat haze) is the wavy distortion you see rising from hot summer pavement — a signature image of Japanese summer poetry, sports anime, and everything that wants to feel sweaty and bright at once.

translations.en: Voices echo back and forth, shoulders slapping each other
translations.es: Voces que se hacen eco, hombros que chocan
translations.pt-BR: Vozes se respondendo, ombros se batendo

literal_meaning.en: Echo-each-other voices, slap-each-other shoulders

cultural_context.en: Verb stem + あう ('do mutually') gives reciprocal verbs: 響きあう, 叩きあう. The hand-on-shoulder slapping is the iconic team-sports image — male sports culture in two strokes.

translations.en: Through the open window, I asked the sky
translations.es: Por la ventana abierta, le pregunté al cielo
translations.pt-BR: Pela janela aberta, eu perguntei pro céu

literal_meaning.en: Opened window from, sky to asked

tokens.reading: ミスターフューチャー

translations.en: Us — this summer — how's it gonna go? Hey, Mr. Future?
translations.es: Nosotros — este verano — ¿cómo va a salir? Oye, Mr. Future
translations.pt-BR: A gente — esse verão — como é que vai ser? Ei, Mr. Future?

literal_meaning.en: We this summer how-is, hey Mr. Future

cultural_context.en: 〜なんだい is a masculine question ending — softer than 〜だ but still casual/rough. Common in 'old buddy' speech and shounen anime. 'Mr. Future' personifies the unknown season ahead.

translations.en: Oh, come on, come on, come on — even a slim chance,
translations.es: Oh, venga, venga, venga — incluso la más mínima oportunidad,
translations.pt-BR: Oh, vai, vai, vai — mesmo a menor chance,

literal_meaning.en: Oh come on come on come on, slight even chance

cultural_context.en: わずかでも = 'even a tiny amount of'. Standard sports/never-give-up phrasing — taking even a slim chance and running with it.

translations.en: Oh, come on — connect it, keep it alive
translations.es: Oh, venga — encadénala, mantenla viva
translations.pt-BR: Oh, vai — segura essa, mantém viva

literal_meaning.en: Oh come on come on come on, connect

cultural_context.en: 繋ぐ ('to connect') is the Haikyuu-friendly verb for 'keep the rally going' — passing the ball one more time, refusing to let it die. Iconic for the show.

meaning.en: wanting to stand (= 立ちたくて)

translations.en: Anytime, anyone — wanting so bad to stand on that stage
translations.es: Siempre, cualquiera — queriendo tanto estar allí
translations.pt-BR: A qualquer hora, qualquer um — querendo tanto estar lá

literal_meaning.en: Anytime anyone, there at want-to-stand-and

cultural_context.en: 〜くって is a casual, slightly emphatic version of the te-form 〜くて (used with adjectives and 〜たい): 立ちたくって = 立ちたくて. Adds emotional double-take, common in shouted lyrics.

translations.en: Messing up, getting mad, never stopping flailing
translations.es: Equivocándonos, irritándonos, sin dejar de bregar
translations.pt-BR: Errando, se irritando, sem parar de se debater

literal_meaning.en: Mistake, get-irritated, struggle-continue

cultural_context.en: もがく = 'to struggle, thrash about' — like a fish out of water. Pairs naturally with 苦しむ ('suffer'), 焦る ('be panicked'), 暴れる ('thrash'). Stronger than 頑張る.

translations.en: Never give up — I don't wanna let it end like this
translations.es: Never give up — no quiero que acabe así
translations.pt-BR: Never give up — não quero acabar assim

literal_meaning.en: Never give up, this-as-is end-want as-for not

cultural_context.en: 終わりたくはない uses the emphatic は ('as for ending — no'): stronger than 終わりたくない. The は inserts a contrast: 'whatever else, I don't want it to END (like this)'.

translations.en: Carrying this imagination, I'm going
translations.es: Cargando esta imaginación, allá voy
translations.pt-BR: Carregando essa imaginação, eu vou

literal_meaning.en: This imagination (object) carrying, I (topic) go (assertion)

cultural_context.en: 抱える = 'to hold something cumbersome / carry on one's back'. Used both literally (抱える荷物) and emotionally (不安を抱える 'carry anxieties'). The imagination here is something you bear forward like a heavy bag.

translations.en: More than the answers found in textbooks
translations.es: Más que las respuestas del libro
translations.pt-BR: Mais que as respostas que estão no livro

literal_meaning.en: Textbook in exists answer than, more

translations.en: I'd been craving knock-your-socks-off feelings
translations.es: Yo ansiaba emociones brutales, fuera de lo común
translations.pt-BR: Eu queria emoções fora do comum

literal_meaning.en: Knocked-flying emotion (object) was-wanting

cultural_context.en: ぶっ〜 is a slangy intensifier prefix from ぶつ ('to hit'). ぶっ飛ぶ = 'to be blown away'; ぶっ飛んだ感動 = 'knock-you-flat emotion'. Other examples: ぶっ壊す ('smash to bits'), ぶっちぎり ('absolute lead').

translations.en: Something that goes 'gwaaah' surging up inside
translations.es: Algo que sube borboteando, en plan 'GWAAAH'
translations.pt-BR: Algo que vem com força — tipo 'GWAAAH'

literal_meaning.en: Welling-up come, GWAAH (quote) something (subject)

cultural_context.en: グワァー is a mimetic noise (giseigo) — the sound of a sudden surge or roar. Putting って after it makes the noise itself the descriptor: 'a GWAAH-style something'. Quintessentially shounen energy.

meaning.en: can believe (= 信じられる, ら抜き)

translations.en: Back then, you were everything I could believe in, Mr. Future
translations.es: En aquel entonces, eras todo en lo que podía creer, Mr. Future
translations.pt-BR: Naquela época, você era tudo em que eu acreditava, Mr. Future

literal_meaning.en: That time, can-believe everything was, Mr. Future

cultural_context.en: 信じれる is the colloquial 'ら抜き' (ra-dropped) potential form of 信じる — proper Japanese is 信じられる. Common in casual speech; technically incorrect but very widespread.

meaning.en: can be heard (= 聞こえている)

translations.en: Oh, hello — you hearing this?
translations.es: Oh, hola — ¿me oyes?
translations.pt-BR: Oh, alô — está ouvindo aí?

literal_meaning.en: Oh hello hello hello, can-hear-am (question)

cultural_context.en: 〜かい is a casual masculine question particle, gentler than 〜だ but still distinctly old-school male. Common in older men's speech and shounen anime.

translations.en: Oh, hello — give me an answer
translations.es: Oh, hola — dame una respuesta
translations.pt-BR: Oh, alô — me dá uma resposta

literal_meaning.en: Oh hello hello hello, answer

translations.en: Bumping into things, rolling around, just wanting to get stronger
translations.es: Chocando, rodando, queriendo hacerme más fuerte
translations.pt-BR: Esbarrando, rolando pelo chão, querendo ficar mais forte

literal_meaning.en: Collide-and, roll-and, strong become-want-and

translations.en: Holding stubborn pride, getting back up — over and over again
translations.es: Aferrándome al orgullo, levantándome — repitiéndolo una y otra vez
translations.pt-BR: Insistindo, levantando de novo — repetindo isso o tempo todo

literal_meaning.en: Stubbornness-stretch-and stand-up-and, repeat but

cultural_context.en: 意地を張る ('to stretch one's pride') means 'to be stubborn out of pride / dig your heels in'. Often disapproving ('don't be so stubborn'), but in sports lyrics it's celebrated.

translations.en: Never give up — just let me keep running
translations.es: Never give up — déjame seguir corriendo
translations.pt-BR: Never give up — deixa eu seguir correndo

literal_meaning.en: Never give up, this-as-is let-run give

cultural_context.en: 走らせてくれ ('let me run') is a causative + くれる ('do for me'). Standard 'permit me' construction: 行かせてくれ ('let me go'), 飲ませてくれ ('let me drink'). The よ caps it with insistence.

translations.en: Beyond this imagination — I'm going
translations.es: Más allá de esta imaginación — allá voy
translations.pt-BR: Pra além dessa imaginação — eu vou

literal_meaning.en: This imagination's beyond toward, I (topic) go (assertion)

cultural_context.en: イマジネーションの先 ('the place beyond imagination') is the song's signature image: pushing past what you could even picture being possible.

meaning.en: has started (= 始まっているんだ)

translations.en: From the moment we lost — the next round's already begun
translations.es: Desde el momento en que perdimos — la siguiente ya ha empezado
translations.pt-BR: Desde o momento em que perdemos — a próxima rodada já começou

literal_meaning.en: Lost time from, next (subject) has-started

cultural_context.en: 始まってんだ contracts 始まっているんだ ('the thing is, it has started'). Common in male spoken speech, lyrics, and motivational anime monologues.

translations.en: Even if right now it tastes bitter and sour, baby — someday, surely
translations.es: Aunque ahora sepa amargo y áspero, baby — algún día, seguro
translations.pt-BR: Mesmo que agora o gosto seja amargo e adstringente, baby — algum dia, com certeza

literal_meaning.en: Now (topic) bitter astringent taste even, baby someday surely

cultural_context.en: 苦い (bitter, like coffee) and 渋い (astringent, like green tea or unripe persimmons) cover two distinct unpleasant tastes. Pairing them = 'an emotionally rough flavor that's not just one kind of bad'.

grammar_points.name: Verb stem + あう (do mutually / each other)

explanation.en: Adding 合う (あう) to a verb stem creates a reciprocal verb meaning 'do X to each other'. 響きあう ('echo each other'), 叩きあう ('slap each other'), 助けあう ('help each other'), 分かりあう ('understand each other'). Productive — works on most action verbs.
explanation.es: Añadir 合う (あう) a la raíz verbal crea un verbo recíproco 'hacerse X mutuamente'. 響きあう, 叩きあう, 助けあう, 分かりあう. Patrón productivo — funciona con la mayoría de verbos de acción.
explanation.pt-BR: Acrescentar 合う (あう) à raiz verbal cria um verbo recíproco 'fazer X um ao outro'. 響きあう, 叩きあう, 助けあう, 分かりあう. Padrão produtivo — funciona com a maioria dos verbos de ação.

grammar_points.name: Casual emphatic 〜くって / 〜って (= 〜くて / 〜て)

explanation.en: Casual speech doubles the consonant in te-form for emphasis: 立ちたくて → 立ちたくって ('really wanting to stand'); なりたくて → なりたくって. Adds a slightly exaggerated, emotional feel — common in shouted lyrics and rough speech.
explanation.es: El habla casual duplica la consonante de la forma -te para enfatizar: 立ちたくて → 立ちたくって; なりたくて → なりたくって. Aporta un matiz exagerado, frecuente en letras gritadas y habla brusca.
explanation.pt-BR: A fala casual duplica a consoante na forma -te para dar ênfase: 立ちたくて → 立ちたくって; なりたくて → なりたくって. Acrescenta tom levemente exagerado, comum em letras gritadas e fala rude.

explanation.en: ぶっ comes from ぶつ ('to hit') and acts as an emphatic prefix on action verbs: ぶっ飛ぶ ('to be blown away / fly off'), ぶっ壊す ('to smash to bits'), ぶっちぎり ('absolute lead'), ぶっつける ('to smack into'). Adds a 'forcefully / wildly' flavor.
explanation.es: ぶっ procede de ぶつ ('golpear') y actúa como prefijo enfático en verbos de acción: ぶっ飛ぶ ('salir volando'), ぶっ壊す ('destrozar'), ぶっちぎり ('liderazgo arrasador'). Aporta tono 'con fuerza / a lo loco'.
explanation.pt-BR: ぶっ vem de ぶつ ('bater') e funciona como prefixo enfático em verbos de ação: ぶっ飛ぶ ('voar pelos ares'), ぶっ壊す ('destruir'), ぶっちぎり ('liderança esmagadora'). Dá tom 'com força / sem freios'.

grammar_points.name: Causative + くれ ('let me / permit me')

explanation.en: Verb-causative + くれ asks 'please let me do X'. 走らせてくれ ('let me run'); 行かせてくれ ('let me go'); 言わせてくれ ('let me speak'). The combination of causative ('make me / let me') + くれる ('do for me') creates a request to be permitted action.
explanation.es: Verbo-causativo + くれ pide 'déjame hacer X'. 走らせてくれ, 行かせてくれ, 言わせてくれ. La combinación causativo + くれる ('hacer por mí') crea una petición de permiso.
explanation.pt-BR: Verbo-causativo + くれ pede 'deixe-me fazer X'. 走らせてくれ, 行かせてくれ, 言わせてくれ. A combinação causativo + くれる ('fazer por mim') gera um pedido de permissão.

grammar_points.name: Casual contraction 〜てんだ (= 〜ているんだ)

explanation.en: Spoken Japanese drops syllables: 〜ているんだ → 〜てるんだ → 〜てんだ. 始まってんだ = 始まっているんだ ('the thing is, it has started'). Adds explanatory tone (んだ) to a progressive (〜ている). Heavily masculine in flavor.
explanation.es: El japonés hablado omite sílabas: 〜ているんだ → 〜てるんだ → 〜てんだ. 始まってんだ = 始まっているんだ ('lo que pasa es que ya empezó'). Tono explicativo (んだ) sobre un progresivo. Sabor masculino marcado.
explanation.pt-BR: O japonês falado omite sílabas: 〜ているんだ → 〜てるんだ → 〜てんだ. 始まってんだ = 始まっているんだ ('é que já começou'). Tom explicativo (んだ) num progressivo (〜ている). Forte sabor masculino.

grammar_points.name: ら抜き (ra-dropped potential): 信じれる, 食べれる, 見れる

explanation.en: Strict potential of ichidan verbs adds 〜られる: 信じる → 信じられる ('can believe'). In casual speech the ら is often dropped: 信じれる, 食べれる, 見れる. Considered grammatically incorrect by purists but extremely widespread, especially among younger speakers.
explanation.es: El potencial estricto de los verbos ichidan añade 〜られる: 信じる → 信じられる. En el habla informal se suele omitir el ら: 信じれる, 食べれる, 見れる. Técnicamente incorrecto, pero generalizado, sobre todo entre jóvenes.
explanation.pt-BR: O potencial estrito de verbos ichidan adiciona 〜られる: 信じる → 信じられる. Na fala casual, o ら costuma ser omitido: 信じれる, 食べれる, 見れる. Tecnicamente incorreto, mas muito difundido na fala jovem.

grammar_points.name: Emphatic は in negative: 〜たくはない

explanation.en: Inserting は into a negative form adds emphasis/contrast: 終わりたくない ('I don't want it to end') → 終わりたくはない ('I really don't want it — least of all — to end like this'). The は singles out the final element as the un-wanted thing.
explanation.es: Insertar は en una forma negativa añade énfasis/contraste: 終わりたくない → 終わりたくはない ('precisamente no quiero que acabe así'). は singulariza el elemento como lo NO deseado.
explanation.pt-BR: Inserir は numa forma negativa enfatiza/contrasta: 終わりたくない → 終わりたくはない ('especificamente não quero acabar assim'). は destaca o elemento como aquilo que NÃO se quer.
